We’re still founder-led, and making that partnership possible for every family is still our mission.

Today, more than 42,000 schools in all 50 states use ParentSquare to reach the parents and guardians of more than 22 million students. Families receive messages in 190+ languages on the channels they prefer, including app, text, email, and phone. Our all-in-one platform brings together communications, attendance, forms, payments, and websites to simplify how schools and families connect and take action. ParentSquare Intelligence, the AI and data layer built into ParentSquare, turns engagement and attendance data into insights that guide proactive outreach, so districts can offer families the right support at the right time.

We’ve been named to the Inc. 5000 list of America’s fastest-growing private companies four years running and to Inc.’s Best Workplaces list two years in a row. We’re committed to our customers and our people, and we’d love for you to help build what’s next.

Who we’re looking for:

Our customers are public school districts and state agencies, and getting paid by them means working through procurement portals, purchase orders, and requirements that differ from one district to the next.

ParentSquare is seeking a Billing Specialist to keep our invoicing accurate and our revenue protected from contract to cash. You'll run day-to-day invoicing, own the billing support queue, and manage portal submissions and collections for some of our largest districts. You'll be a primary contact for customer billing questions and partner closely with Revenue Operations and Renewals to catch and fix deal discrepancies before they turn into invoice problems. This is a detail-heavy, high-volume role on our Accounting team, and the accuracy you bring shows up directly in our cash flow and in how schools experience working with us.

Above all, you'll bring our two permissions to play:

  • Humility. We're heads-down builders who'd rather let the work speak. You ask questions early when a deal doesn't add up, own your fixes, and treat RevOps, Renewals, and Customer Success as teammates working toward the same clean close.
  • Passion for our mission. Every hour a district business office spends untangling a billing issue is an hour not spent on students. Clean, accurate billing makes ParentSquare easy to work with, so schools can stay focused on families.

In This Role You'll:

  • Prepare, create, and send accurate customer invoices that match contract schedules and customer terms
  • Manage the billing support queue in Zendesk, including attaching purchase orders, resending invoices, and updating billing details after contract changes

  • Reconcile transactions in Maxio and across Maxio, our CRM, and NetSuite so balances reflect accurate financial activity

We're looking for someone who has:

Bonus points for:

  • Experience navigating public sector or school district vendor portals
  • NetSuite experience
  • HubSpot experience
  • Background in EdTech or K-12

Why join us?

At ParentSquare, we believe in winning together and building a product that truly serves schools, educators, and families. We value transparency, collaboration, and an entrepreneurial spirit, and we look for team members who share these values. You'll have the opportunity to protect revenue integrity across thousands of school customers, influence a fast-growing company, and make a meaningful impact on K-12 education.

The perks of working for us are great! You'll get your foot in the door as our company continues to grow. We're big believers in work-life balance and provide:

  • Stock options

jobs.description:
Portcast is a venture-backed, Singapore-based logistics technology startup building a real-time transportation visibility platform for global supply chains. We help shippers, manufacturers, and logistics service providers turn data into decisions and decisions into measurable business impact.

Our platform goes beyond visibility. Portcast enables action at scale by surfacing the right risks early, helping teams prevent detention and demurrage, accelerate exception management, and close invoices faster with built-in evidence. We turn visibility into outcomes: reduced costs, improved operational control, and more predictable supply chains.

Founded in 2018 and backed by leading technology investors, we are building for an industry at a critical inflection point of digital transformation. Our team of software engineers, data scientists, and logistics experts is on a mission to make supply chains not just visible, but decisively actionable: end to end.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

Portcast runs on data, our engine predicts when, where, why, and by how many days a container will be delayed, and our customers trust those predictions to make actionable decisions. That trust depends on the data underneath being clean, connected, and reliable.

As our Data Analyst Intern, you'll join the Data team and work closely with our Data Analysts and Data Scientists, reporting to our Data Lead. Your focus will be on data integrations and quality, connecting new data sources into our system, checking the data we ingest for gaps and anomalies, and supporting the QA and automation work that keeps our predictions accurate. This is a hands-on learning role: you won't just be handed a checklist. When something in the data looks off, we'll want you to dig into why, not just flag it. Curiosity and effort matter more here than knowing everything already and exceptional A+ player interns have a real path to a permanent role.

WHAT YOU'LL OWN:

  • Check ingested and system-generated data for anomalies and gaps, and help trace them to the source.

  • Help build and run QA checks, report generation, and automations using Python and SQL.

  • Assist the Data Analysts on day-to-day customer data queries and dashboard upkeep.

  • Support new data-source integrations, connecting carrier and market data into our system, with guidance from the team.

  • Document what you build and what you find, so the team can rely on and reuse your work.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR:

  • Currently pursuing (Final-year student) or recently completed a degree in Computer Science, Data Analytics, Data Science, Engineering, Information Technology, Statistics, or a related field.

  • Working knowledge of Python and SQL, you don't need years of experience, but you should be able to write a query and a script and want to get sharper fast.

  • Prior internship experience in a Data Analyst or Business Analyst role, preferably in a product-based, lean startup particularly in logistics, ecommerce or B2B SaaS data-heavy domain.

  • Willing to learn over "already knows everything": we hire interns for curiosity and effort. You put in the work to understand our domain, product, data, and customers.

  • Curious by Default: when the data surprises you, you chase the why. You ask good questions early and treat every gap as something worth understanding.

  • You own your output, AI included. You can use AI tools to move faster, but you read and validate what they produce, you don't just paste it. If one day the tool isn't there, you can still write the query yourself. You can explain what you did and why, without saying "the AI did it."

  • An eye for detail: you notice when a number looks wrong before anyone else does.

  • Empathy and urgency: you understand that clean data is what customers are counting on, and you move promptly day to day.

  • Fluent in written and verbal English, and comfortable working in a diverse, fully remote team.

WHAT'S IN IT FOR YOU:

  • Real work from day one: you'll touch live data and integrations that customers actually depend on.

  • Mentorship: you'll learn directly from our Data Analysts and Data Scientists.

  • A path to permanent: strong & exceptional A+ player interns here have a real shot at converting to a full-time role.

  • Globally distributed, lean team remote-first flexibility: work with a fully distributed team across Asia and Europe, built on trust, accountability, and collaboration.

Our CORE Values Guide Everything We Do:

jobs.excerpt: About the Job Colorado Christian University is a teaching institution that emphasizes exceptional faculty teaching and achievement of student learning outcomes, within the framework of spiritual formation, as the highest priority.
jobs.description:
About the Job

Colorado Christian University is a teaching institution that emphasizes exceptional faculty teaching and achievement of student learning outcomes, within the framework of spiritual formation, as the highest priority. Affiliate faculty for the PhD in Counselor Education and Supervision program are highly qualified professionals with an earned doctorate in counselor education, preferably from a CACREP-accredited program. They are able to integrate their Christian faith in the classroom to disciple the next generation of Christian leaders in the professional counseling profession.

Job Location

Remote - must reside and work legally in the U.S. All work must be performed within the U.S.
The primary role of the affiliate faculty is teaching, which focuses on instruction, assessment of student learning outcomes, and program evaluation. Most courses are offered in an accelerated format with synchronous and asynchronous components. Core courses are taught using blended formats designed for adult learners. The PhD in Counselor Education and Supervision program is a year-round program.
This is not a full-time position.
An Affiliate Faculty position (often called Adjunct Faculty in higher education) with CCU can be for either our College of Adult and Graduate Studies (CAGS) or College of Undergraduate Studies (CUS).
This is an opening for CAGS, which typically offers classes in an online environment using our Learning Management System (Brightspace).
Upon submitting a resume and application, those candidates who are selected for the next steps are offered the opportunity to complete a one-way video interview. This video interview is reviewed by the Human Resources department and then sent to the appropriate dean for further review. Each dean has a review and selection process, which may include in-person interviews or evaluations. All candidates will be notified of the outcome of the hiring process.
Those who are selected join the CAGS Affiliate Faculty pool and are vetted to teach courses based on their qualifications and relevant experience. Offers for courses are determined based on student enrollment and on how many other faculty are in their respective area of expertise.
Affiliates are expected to learn about CCU and its policies through the University’s Faculty Development team where each Affiliate Faculty member is asked to complete a series of badges to show they have completed the training required to teach at CCU. Affiliates must complete the required badge training to remain in the teaching pool.
All affiliates are paid on a per-class contract basis and are classified as affiliate employees of CCU; affiliates are not considered regular part-time employees. This does afford each affiliate the option to participate in the 403(b) plan, but affiliate faculty are not eligible for any matching contribution and are not eligible for other CCU benefits.

About CCU

Colorado Christian University is the premier interdenominational Christian university in Colorado and the Rocky Mountain region, delivering world class education to thousands of students. The fully accredited, nonprofit University is located in Lakewood, Colorado, a suburb of Denver.
Colorado Christian University was founded in 1914 on two principles — grace and truth. CCU’s scriptural foundation comes from John 1:17: For the law was given through Moses; grace and truth came through Jesus Christ. (ESV)
CCU's mission is Christ-centered higher education transforming students to impact the world with grace and truth.
A leader in higher education, the University has been consistently ranked in the top 2 percent of colleges and universities nationwide for its core curriculum by the American Council of Trustees and Alumni. CCU has had nine consecutive years of enrollment growth and has been named one of the five fastest-growing master’s granting universities byThe Chronicle of Higher Education.
CCU offers more than 200-degree program options for traditional and adult students through its College of Undergraduate Studies and College of Adult and Graduate Studies. More than 9,000 students attend the University on the main campus, in regional centers throughout Colorado, and online.
Scripture states all Christians are called to serve Christ and to minister to others. Because Christians are individuals with different gifts and callings, we serve Christ in a variety of ministry vocations. CCU invites you to explore how you may use your calling and gifts at the University.

What is most appealing about working at CCU?
  1. Faith friendly: CCU’s culture is unique to higher education. Where else can you pursue academic excellence yet read the Holy Bible, pray with teammates and students at work, and work to impact our culture in support of Christian values?
  2. Convictionally Christian: As a university, we have an enduring commitment to Christ, his kingdom and the truth of God’s Word.
  3. Live out your calling: We are a traditional evangelical university where you can invest your God-given talents and abilities alongside coworkers and teammates, while having a profound influence on students as they deepen their relationship with Jesus Christ.
  4. Equip students for kingdom work: You can be a part of helping students discover their callings and preparing them for positions of significant leadership in the church, business, government, education, and other professions, as a key part of our University's Strategic Priorities.

We’re looking for candidates who have:

  1. Doctoral degree in counselor education and supervision, preferably from a CACREP accredited program.
  2. Minimum 2-4 years of teaching experience in the graduate level counseling program
  3. Clinical experience appropriate for graduate and doctoral level instruction.
  4. Appropriate certification and/or licensure (e.g., LPC, LMHC)
  5. Knowledge and demonstrated application of adult learning theory in the classroom.
  6. A record of active scholarship, including peer-reviewed publications or presentations at professional conferences.
  7. Knowledge of ethical standards of practice for professional counseling and counselor education and supervision.
  8. Superior oral, interpersonal, and written communication skills. Ability to work cooperatively within the CCU community.
  9. Desire to be proficient in technological course assets and proficiency in appropriate Microsoft Office software is required.

Preferred Qualifications:

  1. Prior experience in curriculum development and CACREP program accreditation.
  2. Experience in supervising and mentoring masters or doctoral students, on quantitative, qualitative, or mixed methods research projects.
  3. Extensive experience in counselor supervision
  4. Leadership roles in professional counseling organizations.

Key Job Duties:

  1. Contribute to CCU’s mission: Christ-centered higher education transforming students to impact the world with grace and truth. In this role, the PhD in CES faculty will contribute to the University’s mission beyond the classroom through activities such as committee/task force/teamwork, community development, or similar activities internally and externally, which enhance and advance exemplary academics, personal spiritual growth, and engagement with the world.
  2. Meet the expectations of the role of university faculty as defined in the CCU Faculty Handbook, the CAGS Faculty Handbook, and PhD-CES faculty job description.
  3. Participate in affiliate faculty development opportunities
  4. Prepare and teach courses per CAGS standards and expectations. Utilize Brightspace learning platform and other assigned technologies.
  5. Assess, validate, and make recommendations for student learning and for the PhD-CES program, per PhD-CES Assessment Plan, to ensure continuous quality improvement.
  6. Identify with the counseling profession (1) through sustained memberships in professional counseling organizations, (2) through the maintenance of certifications and/or licenses related to their counseling specialty area(s), and (3) by showing evidence of sustained (a) professional development and renewal activities related to counseling, (b) professional services and advocacy in counseling, (c) research and scholarly activity in counseling commensurate with their faculty role.
  7. Maintain clinical competency in their area of specialty practice.
  8. Adhere to professional standards as established by state governing bodies, the American Counseling Association (ACA) Code of Ethics, Association for Counselor Education and Supervision (ACES) best practices, and CACREP standards.

Work Environment

While performing the duties of this job, you may be required to walk, stand, sit, reach with hands and arms, balance, stoop, speak with clarity, and have appropriate vision and hearing capabilities. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds. You may be required to work occasional irregular hours, including some nights and weekends.

Affiliate Faculty pay is typically $400-$600 per credit hour for undergraduate classes and $1,000 per credit hour for graduate level classes. Details regarding payment for low-enrolled courses are included in course contracts.

Join us on this journey and let’s build the future of finance together!

What is this role about?

As the Senior Social & Content Manager, you´ll lead social end-to-end across our markets, own the editorial calendar and content distribution engine, and run the creator program. You´ll partner with Brand & Creative, Product Marketing, Performance, and Country teams to make content a measurable lever for demand generation at Bondora.

You´ll be joining the team at a time when we're reimagining how engaging, high-quality content is built in the AI era. Humans and AI agents operating as one system, producing faster, sharper, multi-platform work that wouldn't have been possible just a few years ago.

We're looking for someone who lives and breathes great content and knows how to make it travel. Someone inspired by what the best brands do across every surface they own, and who sees content not as individual pieces but as a propagation engine that compounds reach.

You bring strong editorial taste. You know how social media actually works today, and you treat content atomization as a discipline: one piece, many executions, each earning its place. You think about distribution before production, imagining how every asset travels across owned, earned, and creator channels to drive measurable demand.

Your main responsibilities will be:

  • Leading Bondora's social media end-to-end across all markets, elevating social into a measurable growth channel.
  • Owning the editorial calendar and content distribution engine: planning content across owned, earned, and creator surfaces, atomising each brand activation into platform-native formats.
  • Producing content in-house in collaboration with the Brand team, alongside managing social and content production agencies and UGC creators end-to-end: sourcing, briefing, quality control, performance management, and cost efficiency.
  • Architecting and operating Bondora's AI-driven content engine: building the systems, tools, and workflows, and running them day-to-day across ideation, editorial planning, production, repurposing, social listening, and performance analysis, continuously raising the output bar through iteration and feedback loops.
  • Running social, content, and share-of-voice analytics and turning channel, format, and audience data into editorial and distribution decisions.
  • Managing social media community day-to-day: moderating and responding to comments and messages across channels.

What would ensure success in this role?

  • 6–10 years of experience in social media, editorial, content, or content marketing roles, ideally within fintech, consumer tech, or another fast-paced digital business.
  • Proven hands-on experience with AI-driven content workflows. You’ve either built an AI-enabled content engine yourself or operated one deeply enough to explain the systems, tools, workflows, and measurable business impact behind it.
  • Strong editorial judgment and creative taste. You know what makes content distinctive, on-brand, relevant, and worth sharing, especially when AI produces at scale.
  • Senior-level social media expertise across multiple platforms, with a strong understanding of platform-native formats, audience behaviour, algorithms, and content mechanics across TikTok, YouTube and Shorts, Meta, and LinkedIn.
  • Strong analytical capability across social and content performance, share of voice, distribution, and attribution. You can turn data into clear decisions about what to create, where to distribute it, and what to scale.
  • Experience building and managing external content ecosystems, including briefing and managing agencies, UGC creators, influencers or creators, and external editors or production partners.
  • Balance of editorial craft and systems thinking, with the ability to work comfortably across marketing, performance, product, and data teams.

What can you expect at Bondora?

  • Contribute to Bondora’s ambitious goal of reaching 1BN in revenue by the end of 2029. Your skills and efforts will directly impact our growth trajectory and shape the future of our company.
  • Our employees deserve the best. We recognize our people with a competitive salary and a generous benefits package (5 weeks of vacation, private healthcare compensation, €1,200 hobby grant, mental healthcare support, share options and much more!)
  • We provide an environment that encourages your personal and professional growth. As we constantly evolve and innovate, you’ll have endless opportunities (and budget) to expand your skills and skyrocket your career.

The next steps

If you have the guts, ideas, and a team vision, apply now!

Our hiring process:

  • Meet Kerli, our Recruiter: Share your experiences and aspirations.
  • Collaborate with Daria, our hiring manager: Learn more about the role.
  • Put your skills to the test: Tackle a home task to showcase your skills.
  • Assessments: Complete our personality and logic assessments.

About the role

This role is the analytical and operational link between AssetWatch’s business stakeholders and the Revenue Systems delivery team. The right person brings genuine business analysis instincts — the ability to surface requirements, resolve competing priorities, and translate complex business needs into something a development team can execute — alongside the organizational discipline to keep a fast-moving sprint cadence on track.

What's the opportunity

Requirements Gathering and Business Analysis

You will lead structured discovery sessions with stakeholders across Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, Marketing Operations, Customer Success Operations, Engineering, and Product — not just attending them but facilitating them. That means surfacing unstated assumptions, identifying conflicting requirements before they reach development, and documenting what was agreed to with enough precision that the team can build from it without circling back. You will translate those conversations into well-formed user stories with clear acceptance criteria, evaluate solution options against real business constraints, and flag trade-offs before work begins.

Stakeholder Alignment and Conflict Resolution

Multiple teams will often bring competing priorities and different interpretations of what a system should do. You will own the alignment work — getting the right people in the room, making trade-offs visible, and resolving conflicts before they become delivery delays. That includes keeping sprint commitments transparent to dependent teams and managing expectations proactively when scope or timelines need to shift. This role operates across many teams and inbound requests simultaneously — strong organizational habits and the ability to carry multiple priorities forward at once without losing momentum on any of them are part of what makes someone successful here.

Process Improvement and UAT

You will document current-state business processes, identify opportunities for automation and workflow improvement, and own the full UAT lifecycle for every enhancement before it reaches production. That means writing test scripts, coordinating business reviewers, triaging defects, and confirming sign-off before any deployment goes live.

Sprint Operations and User Support

You will manage the Jira backlog, run sprint planning and daily standups, follow up before sprint deadlines, and send action items and release notes after each deployment. You will also triage inbound Salesforce support requests through the team’s Slack channel, acknowledge requests promptly, route issues appropriately, and keep stakeholders informed throughout.

What we're looking for

  • 3+ years in a BSA, Revenue Operations, or Salesforce-adjacent role in a B2B SaaS environment

  • Comfortable navigating competing stakeholder priorities and resolving cross-team conflicts

Job Title: Customer Success Manager

Location: Remote

Job Scope:

We are seeking an experienced Customer Success Manager to own and drive the success of our customers using

our SaaS products. This role emphasizes customer satisfaction, product adoption, feature enablement, proactive

customer health management, SLA and SOP adherence and identification of opportunities to continuously improve

the customer experience. The ideal candidate will be a proactive, commercially aware and customer-centric

professional who can build strong customer relationships, anticipate customer needs, coordinate effectively with

internal teams and identify and close paid Change Request (CR) and expansion opportunities.

Responsibilities:

  • Customer Relationship and Success Management:

Act as the primary point of contact for assigned customers, build trusted long-term relationships, understand

customer objectives and challenges, conduct regular customer touchpoints and business reviews, own

customer success plans and proactively identify and mitigate customer risks.

• Product Adoption and Usage Monitoring:

Measure and monitor product and feature adoption, identify underutilized capabilities or declining usage,

establish adoption metrics and work with customers to increase usage and demonstrate greater business value

from the product.

  • Feature Enablement and Continuous Improvement:

Stay aligned with product releases and proactively identify new features relevant to each customer. Drive

feature enablement through release communication, demonstrations, walkthroughs and customer engagement

so customers continuously benefit from new product capabilities and improvements.

  • Customer Health and System Health Monitoring:

Maintain customer health indicators covering adoption, support trends, SLA performance, system health,

customer sentiment and engagement. Conduct periodic system health checks, identify potential risks or

recurring issues and provide proactive updates and recommendations to customers.

• SLA and Service Delivery Management:

Monitor adherence to agreed SLAs, proactively identify potential breaches or service-level concerns,

coordinate with Support and Engineering teams and ensure customers receive timely and meaningful updates

on incidents, resolution plans and expected timelines.

• SOP and Operational Governance:

Understand and maintain customer-specific Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), governance processes

and agreed ways of working. Ensure agreed SOPs are executed consistently, monitor adherence, identify

deviations and coordinate updates when business processes or product capabilities change.

• Change Request and Revenue Generation:

Proactively identify paid Change Request (CR), enhancement and expansion opportunities. Work with

Product, Implementation and Commercial teams to qualify and scope opportunities, engage customers on

business value and commercial implications and actively pursue identified opportunities through proposal,

negotiation and closure.

  • Customer Feedback and Product Advocacy:

Capture structured customer feedback, pain points and enhancement requests, identify recurring themes and

collaborate with Product teams to ensure customer needs are appropriately considered in product prioritization

and roadmap discussions.

Conduct regular customer success reviews and business reviews covering adoption, system health, SLA

teams to deliver a seamless customer experience. Drive clear ownership, timelines and communication for

cross-functional customer activities and escalations.

Proactively identify churn risks and develop mitigation plans. Monitor customer satisfaction and engagement,

build strong stakeholder relationships and identify opportunities to turn satisfied customers into product

advocates, references and expansion opportunities.

  • Knowledge Management and Continuous Improvement:

Maintain comprehensive customer documentation covering configurations, processes, contacts,

dependencies, SOPs, risks and key decisions. Contribute to knowledge bases and customer collateral and

continuously improve customer success processes based on feedback, data and operational learnings.

similar customer-facing role

and follow-ups

o Ability to proactively identify customer risks, opportunities and areas for improvement

o Strong presentation and business communication skills

o Commercial awareness and ability to identify and pursue revenue opportunities

o Experience working with SLAs, operational processes, service reviews and customer governance

o Proficiency in using computer applications, including the Microsoft Office Suite

o Experience with SaaS products, particularly enterprise SaaS solutions

o Experience with HCM solutions, especially those integrated with SAP SuccessFactors

o Experience managing enterprise customers and senior customer stakeholders

o Familiarity with SAP SuccessFactors and related enterprise application ecosystems

o Understanding of SaaS product adoption, customer health metrics and usage analytics

jobs.description:
About Us

Super Organics is the parent company behind a portfolio of natural wellness supplement brands — including Super Speciosa, Kratom Country, Fully, and Sun Nutra. We’re a growing team based in Fort Lauderdale building brands that people actually buy, use, and come back to.

The Role

We’re hiring a Copywriter & Creative Strategist to be our creative voice across Fully and Sun Nutra, with crossover support for Super Speciosa. You’ll write the emails, ads, product pages, and packaging copy that go out the door — and help shape the ideas and visuals behind them.

This is a role for someone 2–3 years into their career who wants to grow fast. You’ll get real ownership from day one, see your work ship constantly, and sharpen your skills across writing, strategy, and creative direction — the kind of range you can’t get at a bigger company where everyone stays in their lane.

A note on AI: we use it, and we expect you to. It’s a tool for productivity — research, drafts, iteration. What we need is someone whose own voice, taste, and judgment make the work feel human.

This is a remote position.

What You’ll Own

Copywriting

  • Email and SMS copy for Fully, Sun Nutra, and Super Speciosa — promotional sends, lifecycle flows, product launches, retention campaigns
  • Paid social and search ad copy across Meta, Google, and emerging channels
  • Product detail pages, landing pages, and web copy
  • Packaging and on-product copy (hang tags, inserts, back-of-pack)
  • Amazon A+ content and PDP copy for Sun Nutra and other Amazon-present brands
  • Organic social copy where needed, including short-form video scripts and hooks

Creative Strategy & Briefing

  • Concept campaigns from scratch — the idea, the hook, the through-line — not just the copy that wraps someone else’s concept
  • Write clear, inspired creative briefs that set designers, video editors, and agency partners up to do their best work
  • Translate product, positioning, and audience insight into creative direction that actually converts
  • Partner with leadership on seasonal planning, brand activations, and new product launches

Visual Concepting & Light Art Direction

  • Concept visuals alongside your writing — mood boards, reference decks, rough layouts, and shot lists
  • Art-direct designers and video editors (internal and external) toward a clear creative vision
  • Review visual creative for on-brand execution and give useful, specific feedback
  • Think in campaigns, not assets — your PDP imagery should feel related to your email, which should feel related to your ad

Brand Voice Stewardship

  • Maintain and evolve voice guidelines across Fully, Sun Nutra, and Super Speciosa — each brand has a distinct personality and you’ll need to shift between them fluently
  • Review outbound creative against brand standards and flag off-brand work early, even from senior stakeholders
  • Help onboard freelancers and agency partners to each brand’s voice when needed

Who You Are

  • A writer with a real voice — your portfolio sounds like a person, not a template
  • Full of ideas — you come to the table with concepts, not just execution
  • Visually literate — you think in mood boards, references, and campaigns, not just words
  • An AI power user with taste — you use it to move faster, not to avoid the work
  • Hungry to grow — you want mentorship, feedback, and a real path to senior creative work
  • Collaborative — you take feedback well and play nicely with a small team
  • Comfortable in regulated categories like supplements — you respect the guardrails and get creative within them
  • Looking for a long-term home — we’re investing in this hire and want someone who wants to grow with us

Requirements

  • 2–3+ years of copywriting experience (in-house brand, DTC, or agency)
  • A portfolio or writing samples — required, no exceptions
  • Experience concepting campaigns and writing creative briefs
  • Comfort across channels: email, paid social, organic social, web, and packaging
  • Familiarity with the DTC / ecommerce ecosystem (Shopify, Klaviyo, Meta, ideally Amazon)
  • Able to work Monday–Friday, 9 AM to 5 PM EST
  • Legally authorized to work in the U.S.

Nice to Have

  • Background in supplements, wellness, beauty, or CPG
  • Short-form video instincts (TikTok, Reels) — hooks, scripting, trend literacy
  • Working knowledge of Figma or Canva
  • Experience launching a brand or product from zero

Benefits

  • Competitive salary (commensurate with experience)
  • Remote, work from home position
  • Health insurance
  • Paid time off
  • Mentorship and a clear path to grow into senior creative roles

jobs.description:
ABOUT QUINCE

Quince is a destination for builders, creators, innovators, and operators who want to come together and challenge the status quo. Our mission is simple: make really high quality essentials for really low prices, fairly and sustainably. We deliver on that mission through a unique manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) model eliminating the layers of traditional retail that add cost and result in consumers paying more than they need to. We find, build relationships with, and work directly with the manufacturing partners behind some of the world’s finest products. From there, our teams design smart, efficient operational processes and build and deploy proprietary technology, AI, and analytics to help us scale fast.

What began with a small assortment of elevated basics has quickly grown into a cross-category brand spanning apparel, accessories, home goods, and more. Today, tens of millions of people across a growing number of countries come – and return – to Quince because they trust us to deliver.

OUR CULTURE

Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper. We question conventional thinking, use technology and data to uncover new opportunities, and move quickly to turn ideas into reality. We aren’t interested in replicating how others do retail. We’re building a better way – at a speed and scale unlike anything that’s been done before.

  • We dream big and chase the hard problems others shy away from. Rejecting long-held assumptions is part of our company's DNA. Where conventional wisdom says you have to choose – soft or durable, speed or rigor, quality or price – we ask why that trade-off has to exist in the first place.
  • Our pace is fast and the bar is high because our customers expect a lot from us and we refuse to let them down. We believe the best results come from challenging ourselves, learning from one another, and building on each other's strengths.
  • Here, responsibility is not determined by role, tenure, or seniority. Every team member - no matter their level - has the opportunity to drive our business and shape our trajectory.

If you’re someone who likes to imagine new possibilities and build better systems rather than plug-in to outdated ones, Quince is the place for you.

THE ROLE

Sr. Manager, Global Procurement (Hard Home)

We are seeking an exceptional Sr. Manager, Global Procurement (Hard Home) to own and drive cost structures and savings. This role is critical to our goal of delivering the highest quality products, at radically low prices, done right. Reporting to the Head of Procurement, the ideal candidate will leverage their deep expertise in commodity costing, clean sheet, manufacturing excellence & efficiency (consumption, C&M excellence), harvest timing, raw material availability to craft a competitive costing environment where major T1 and T2 suppliers are being challenged to provide transparent and competitive pricing to achieve a win win supply chain for both Quince and our partners.

Success in this role means achieving product cost at or near should-costing, securing supply continuity, and contributing to product excellence by aligning material procurement processes with the company’s innovation and sustainability goals. This role offers the opportunity to make a significant impact on our business,contribute to company growth, and shape the future of our global sourcing strategy.

Responsibilities

  • Procurement Category Strategy: Define and execute the commercial roadmap and vendor distribution strategy for assigned categories to improve margins as Quince scales. Establish short- and long-term procurement targets aligned to business growth.
    • Consistently deliver exceptional product cost without sacrificing product quality or ESG considerations, including Procurement.
    • Partner with the technology team to embed procurement capabilities and playbook into the Vendor Portal and Product Catalog tools.
    • Identify and deliver 700 bps product cost reductions over the next 12 months.
  • RFP Ownership & Execution: Structure and run competitive, end-to-end bidding processes to secure optimal cost and commercial terms with manufacturing partners. Own the full lifecycle from vendor identification through award.
    • Deliver immediate, best-in-class product cost savings through rigorous negotiation, while simultaneously institutionalizing repeatable negotiation frameworks to build long-term category maturity and sustainable competitive advantage.
    • Build AI agent to help us run RFP systematically in 2026 with the capability to build scenario analyses.
  • Clean Sheet & Buy Plan Approvals: Create and utilize component-level “clean sheets” to drive pricing transparency; review, approve, and solution to optimum cost for all buy events within your categories.
    • Current mature / scale categories: Ensure scale / cleansheet costing with Finished GoodsManufacturers Negotiate upstream of Finished Goods to secure best pricing and availability of (inputs (e.g. fabrics, yarns, fibers, commodities, trims) New categories / new products
    • Lead Buy Plan margin review to govern company margin targetPartner with material sourcing team to ensure transparent, competitive pricing from all key material suppliers (we own material, we own costing)
    • Negotiate reasonable launch costing and set schedule (monthly, quarterly, at trigger points) to renegotiate for scale pricing as the business grows
    • Support merchandising team by providing scale costing targets (i.e. what cost is achievable at scale)
  • Upstream Sourcing: Partner directly with the Material Manager, Sourcing Teams and Tier 1 and Tier 2 vendors to align on, and implement, material benefits into finished goods costing.
    • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to integrate upstream material availability into product design and development cycles, ensuring early-stage cost optimization and seamless material-to-finished-good transitions.
  • Value Creation: Identify and execute on opportunities to reshape the supply chain and extract new financial value beyond traditional sourcing boundaries, including verticalization and volume consolidation plays.
    • e.g. How do we become a market maker for Cashmere, Silk, etc? Could we sell cashmere and silk to other retailers? How can we partner with other mills or manufacturers to build a verticalized supply chain for critical materials, like linen, from French/Belgian farms and scutchers to linen mills? How do we buy/sell commodities to manage price fluctuations (e.g. gold pricing, Cashmere pricing)?

Qualifications

Required:

  • 12-15 years of experience in global procurement, sourcing, or supply chain management in a consumer goods or retail environment
  • Proven track record running competitive RFP processes with international manufacturing partners
  • Hands-on experience building and leveraging clean sheets for cost negotiation
  • Strong analytical skills and comfort with data-driven decision making
  • Experience working cross-functionally with merchandising, materials, and production teams

All posted ranges are reflective of base salary and may vary depending upon experience level and location. Bonus and equity may also be provided for eligible roles.

Pay Range
$164,000—$240,000 USD

WHY QUINCE?

Joining Quince means being part of a mission-driven team reshaping retail. You will work alongside talented colleagues, tackle meaningful challenges, and contribute to building a more sustainable, accessible future for customers and partners alike.

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY & HIRING INTEGRITY

Quince provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applications for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran or military status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws.

Join the GTM Revolution at SalesCaptain — Where B2B Growth Happens

Since our beginnings in 2021, SalesCaptain has grown into a global force, working with fast-growing B2B brands, YC & Techstars startups, and Series B/C companies, helping them go to market through predictable, scalable outbound systems.

We're looking for a Senior GTM Engineer to own and evolve our outbound revenue infrastructure across client accounts.

This is a hands-on senior role sitting at the intersection of data, automation, AI, deliverability, intent signals, and outbound strategy. Beyond building systems yourself, you’ll help set technical standards, introduce new GTM technologies, and mentor other team members.

This is a full-time, remote role, working EU hours.

About the role

You’ll work closely with GTM Strategists, Campaign Managers, and other GTM Engineers to architect scalable outbound systems from ICP definition through campaign execution and reporting.

You’ll own complex Clay workflows, data infrastructure, intent and signal-based targeting, automation, and deliverability, while continuously testing new AI and GTM tools that can improve our results.

We’re looking for someone who can not only build great systems, but also lead technically, challenge existing processes, and help raise the standard of the wider team.

What you’ll do ✨

  • Architect end-to-end outbound systems, from ICP and TAM definition through enrichment, sequencing, CRM sync, and performance reporting
  • Build and optimize advanced Clay workflows, including enrichment waterfalls, Claygent, AI columns, conditional logic, and custom API integrations
  • Own and improve email deliverability infrastructure, including domains, inbox health, sending infrastructure, authentication, reputation, and scaling best practices
  • Design intent and signal-based outbound systems using signals such as job changes, funding, hiring activity, website intent, technology adoption, social activity, and other buying signals
  • Build automation workflows with n8n, Make, Zapier, APIs, and webhooks
  • Use AI and LLMs to improve prospect research, qualification, personalization, data processing, and campaign workflows
  • Continuously explore and test new AI and GTM technologies, identifying tools and approaches that can give SalesCaptain and our clients an advantage
  • Write lightweight Python or JavaScript and work directly with APIs when no-code tools aren’t enough
  • Partner with GTM Strategists to improve targeting, campaign architecture, and outbound performance
  • Establish best practices and documentation for GTM engineering workflows
  • Mentor junior and mid-level GTM Engineers, review workflows, troubleshoot complex problems, and help the team develop technically
  • Proactively identify inefficient processes and design better, more scalable solutions

Requirements

Who you are ❤️‍🔥

You should have:

  • 3+ years of experience in GTM Engineering, RevOps, outbound operations, growth engineering, or a closely related role
  • Strong hands-on experience building outbound systems in a B2B SaaS, GTM agency, consultancy, or fast-moving technology environment
  • Advanced experience with Clay, including complex enrichment workflows, Claygent, AI columns, waterfalls, and APIs
  • Strong understanding of email deliverability, sending infrastructure, domain reputation, authentication, and inbox health
  • Experience designing campaigns around intent data and buying signals, rather than relying only on static prospect lists
  • Strong knowledge of the modern GTM tooling ecosystem and genuine curiosity around emerging AI and automation tools
  • Comfort working with APIs, webhooks, JSON, automation platforms, and basic Python or JavaScript
  • A strong commercial mindset — you understand ICPs, messaging, outbound performance, pipeline, and why targeting decisions matter
  • Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to design systems rather than simply execute predefined tasks
  • Experience mentoring, supporting, or reviewing the work of other team members
  • Excellent English communication skills (C1–C2), with the ability to explain technical concepts clearly to non-technical stakeholders
  • Experience working with Tech, SaaS, or B2B software companies

We’re also open to candidates coming from RevOps, growth engineering, Clay consulting, outbound operations, or highly technical SDR/BDR backgrounds who have transitioned into systems building.

What good looks like

You are successful in this role if:

  • GTM Strategists trust the systems and data you build without needing to recheck everything
  • Our outbound infrastructure remains scalable, reliable, and deliverability-safe
  • Intent signals help us identify better prospects and improve campaign timing
  • Clay and automation workflows are clean, efficient, documented, and cost-effective
  • You regularly introduce new AI, automation, and GTM approaches that improve how the team works
  • You identify problems before they become bottlenecks
  • Other GTM Engineers improve through your mentoring and technical guidance
  • You help the team move faster while maintaining a high standard of data and execution quality

This role is not for you if

  • You have never used Clay or similar GTM automation tools
  • Your outbound experience is limited to basic LinkedIn scraping or list building
  • You have little understanding of email deliverability
  • You prefer executing instructions rather than designing systems and proposing improvements
  • You are not interested in experimenting with new AI and GTM technologies
  • You are uncomfortable taking ownership of complex technical problems
  • You do not enjoy mentoring or sharing knowledge with other team members

Benefits

In addition to joining a fast-growing GTM team, we offer:

  • Remote work
  • Collaborative, friendly, and ambitious team
  • Paid vacation, days off, and sick leave
  • Team-building activities
  • Free books and Kindles to support your development
  • Specialized training and access to leading GTM tools
  • Opportunity to work with international B2B brands, startups, and scaleups
  • Hands-on exposure to emerging AI, automation, data, and GTM technologies
  • Significant autonomy to experiment, introduce new tools, and influence how our GTM infrastructure evolves
  • Opportunity to mentor others and play a key role in developing the GTM Engineering function

About Sidekick

At Sidekick, we help people recover faster from injuries. Trusted by Olympic champions and everyday athletes, our products have been featured in Men's Health and Running Magazine. With 94% of users finding relief, we aim to be the go-to injury relief brand.

The role

A lot of performance creative work goes into creating demand that wasn't there. That's not the problem here. Our customer already wants what we sell. Their heel hurts every morning when they get out of bed, or their ankle rolls on uneven ground and they've stopped trusting it.

What they don't believe is that this is the thing that finally works. They've already bought the insoles, done the stretches, and gone to physio twice. So you have to teach before you can sell, and you have to earn trust from someone who has been let down already. It's a harder brief than most, and a more interesting one.

You'll write our paid social advertising and own angle development and testing, reporting to our Creative Director. Expect to ship around 15 briefs a week, a mix of net-new concepts and iterations on ads that are already working. Your week is writing, research, and feedback to editors.

You don't need a physiotherapy background, but you do need to pick up a clinical concept quickly enough to explain it clearly and honestly in fifteen seconds of camera time.

What you'll do

  • Find new winning angles. Better creative is what lets us spend more, so we need a steady supply of ads that keep working as budgets grow.
  • Open new audiences. Runners, older adults worried about falling, people on their feet all day. Each group buys for a different reason, and every one we crack opens up new demand.
  • Get more life out of winners. Read the data weekly, iterate what's working, retire what's finished.
  • Write the scripts. Short and long-form video, hooks that stop the scroll, dialogue that sounds like a real person. This is most of your week.
  • Direct the edit. Brief and manage editors and creators so the idea survives production.
  • Extend what wins. Take proven angles into landing pages and email.

Requirements

What we're looking for

  • 4+ years writing paid social ads that were judged on sales (not brand awareness, engagement etc.)
  • Your ads have been responsible for over $100K+/month in ad spend (across all your ads, for a single brand). We'll ask you to walk us through it.
  • Proof you can iterate on a winner. Plenty of people can write one good ad; we want someone who gets eight more out of it.
  • You've opened a new audience before, and you can name the angle that got you in
  • Excellent writing for spoken word, which is a different skill from writing for the page
  • Strong direct response fundamentals: offer, mechanism, objection handling, proof
  • Experience briefing editors or creators
  • Health, fitness or medical device categories are a plus

What we care about

We want people who are ambitious and hold themselves to a high standard. They don't need to be managed closely, and want to be the best at their craft. The volume is real and the feedback is direct. In exchange you'll see more results in a year than most people see in three. If you're looking for something comfortable, this won't be the right fit for you.

Benefits

  • Compensation: Top of the market for this role. We’ll share compensation details on the first call.
  • Fast-growing company whose mission is to solve chronic pain and injuries
  • You’ll see the direct impact of your work on business results
  • You’ll be held to a high bar, which means you’ll get better fast
  • Fun, approachable yet ambitious colleagues
  • Comprehensive health benefits
  • Work from home

A lot of performance creative work goes into creating demand that wasn't there. That's not the problem here. Our customer already wants what we sell. Their heel hurts every morning when they get out of bed, or their ankle rolls on uneven ground and they've stopped trusting it.

What they don't believe is that this is the thing that finally works. They've already bought the insoles, done the stretches, and gone to physio twice. You'll write our paid social advertising and own angle development and testing, reporting to our Creative Director. Expect to ship around 15 briefs a week, a mix of net-new concepts and iterations on ads that are already working. Your week is writing, research, and feedback to editors.

You don't need a physiotherapy background, but you do need to pick up a clinical concept quickly enough to explain it clearly and honestly in fifteen seconds of camera time.

Customer-Facing Security Assurance (10%)

jobs.title: Director of Data Science & Engineering, Fraud Platform
jobs.excerpt: Join Zepz: Breaking Down Borders, Together At Zepz, we're all about breaking down barriers for our customers and our teammates.
jobs.description:
Join Zepz: Breaking Down Borders, Together

At Zepz, we're all about breaking down barriers for our customers and our teammates. Our purpose is deeply personal, we provide a lifeline and deliver opportunities to cross-border communities that need it most through cutting edge finance and tech. Zepz is the power behind WorldRemit and Sendwave, driven by the mission to celebrate the incredible impact migrants have, both at home and abroad. We're not just moving money; we're building a world that truly recognizes and supports global connections. Who You'll Be Joining We look for mission-driven builders who thrive in a fast-paced environment connected to a true purpose. We’re an always developing team of experts that enjoy problem solving and bring clarity to tough challenges. At Zepz, we are Relentless Learners, always seeking feedback, and Responsible Owners, treating company resources like our own. We depend on Transparent Communicators who keep the team aligned through open, honest talk.

Our Core Commitments— What We Live By
Our vibrant and truly diverse culture is built on three core commitments, that guide how we work and interact:
  • Integrity: We always do the right thing. It’s simple, but it’s the foundation of everything we build for our customers and each other.
  • Outcomes: We work for our customers. Their success and prosperity are the results we focus on delivering.
  • Velocity: We are fast! We maintain high energy levels and make smart decisions quickly, keeping us nimble and ahead of the curve.
Perks of Joining Our Team
We believe in empowering colleagues because we genuinely trust our team. Our culture is founded on this high trust, which naturally encourages the high ownership that drives us to meet our shared high expectations and deliver high performance. While we have all the tools to work remotely, we value the purpose and benefits of in-person connections so we expect our teams to come together for team off-sites and connects. Alongside a great flexible working environment, think unlimited annual leave , great healthcare benefits, and employee discounts. We want you to thrive and focus entirely on making your biggest impact! In turn, we expect you to bring high ownership and commitment to your work. This is a place where we value trust and high performance, and we'll provide the environment and support needed for you to excel

About the role
This is a high-visibility, high-accountability role — outcomes are reported to C-level and the board, and the role owns both the data strategy and the model performance behind systems that directly protect revenue and customer trust. The mandate in one line: own what data is generated and how it is generated and consumed across the Identity and Financial Crime domains. Almost every consequential decision Zepz makes about a transaction — is this person who they say they are, is this payment safe, is this account compromised — is a decision made on data. Identity is our single largest producer of that data. Financial Crime is our single largest consumer of it. Both sit in the same engineering organization, and today no one owns the path between them. The result is a permanent tax on everything downstream: problems discovered late, by the people least able to fix them at source. This role exists to remove that tax. You will lead a team of 25+ Data Scientists, Machine Learning Engineers and Analytics Engineers across the Identity and Financial Crime domains

What you will own
● Own the definition, generation, quality and consumption of data across the Identity and Financial Crime domains — what gets produced, what it means, what guarantees come with it, and who is accountable when those guarantees are not met.
● Make data quality an engineering discipline rather than a downstream cleanup exercise: producer/consumer contracts, freshness and integrity monitoring, lineage, a named owner for every critical dataset, and a real path from a detected anomaly to a fix at source. You'll be measured on whether downstream teams stop discovering data problems by accident.
● Own the models and analytics behind how Zepz detects fraud and financial crime — feature engineering, model development, deployment, monitoring and retraining. You own model performance in production, not just model development.
● Lead a mixed organization of Data Scientists, Machine Learning Engineers and Analytics Engineers. These are three different crafts with three different career paths, and leading them well means understanding all three rather than favoring the one you came from.
● Partner as a peer with the Engineering Manager who owns the fraud detection platform and reports directly to the VP Engineering. Your models run on their platform: you own model outcomes, they own platform outcomes, and you jointly own the seam between them.
● Partner with our central data function, which owns core data infrastructure and platform tooling. You are a demanding customer and a collaborator, not a replacement — you build domain data products and quality practice on top of what they provide, and feed real requirements back to them.
● Set standards with Identity engineering teams who do not report to you. Much of your impact depends on changing how data is produced upstream, which is influence work: making the cost of poor data visible with evidence rather than assertion, and making it easy for those teams to do the right thing.
● Create high-performing teams with a bias toward shipping without sacrificing reliability or trust in the numbers. Use technical and data debt as a tool to move faster, while ensuring your teams have the space to build it right once they know what the right thing to build is.
● Hire, retain, and level up superlative talent to ensure our team remains world-class as we continue to scale and launch into new markets.
● Roll up your sleeves when models degrade or data breaks. You'll need to discuss technical solutions, review work in depth, and help execute strategy with your leads.

In your first few months, you will:
● Establish an honest, evidenced baseline of data quality across the identity-to-financial-crime path — what breaks, how often, who finds out, and what it costs in downstream hours and model degradation. Bring the number, not the anecdote.
● Agree a written ownership model with the central data team and the Identity engineering leads: who owns which datasets, what the contracts are, and what happens when one is broken.
● Instrument the critical path, so data issues are detected by monitoring rather than by an analyst noticing that something looks odd.
● Get to know the models — how they perform, how they degrade, how retraining actually works today, and where risk is concentrated.
● Assess the team: identify the gaps, the flight risks and the people ready for more, and start hiring against a plan rather than against a vacancy.
● Promote a culture of ownership, accountability, and shipping.

What you bring to the table
● You have a track record of leading a data organization of comparable size (roughly 15–25 people) and of supporting the professional development of managers and senior-level ICs.
● Track record of leading mixed technical teams — Data Scientists, ML Engineers, Analytics Engineers — with genuine credibility across all three crafts.
● Demonstrable ownership of data quality at scale: contracts, observability, lineage, semantic consistency — with evidence of the downstream impact, not just the tooling you installed.
● Fluency with modern lakehouse and analytics engineering practice: Databricks (or equivalent), dbt-style transformation, feature store concepts and real-time feature serving, and the discipline of treating datasets as products with owners and SLAs.
● Experience with production ML in a real-time context: model monitoring, drift detection, and retraining pipelines.
● Proven experience with AWS at scale.
● Direct experience leading FinCrime/Fraud or Identity engineering or data science teams (not just adjacent risk/security).
● The ability to get outcomes from teams that don't report to you. We'd rather hear about a time you changed a producer team's behavior than a time you escalated.
● At least 8+ years of technical experience in a hybrid IC/management role.
● You can attract and retain top talent and lead teams with diverse skill sets.
● You work well with Engineering and Product leaders and are comfortable building effective relationships with folks outside of the Prod-Eng spheres.
● You have exceptional judgment; we're scaling quickly — you'll be required to make good tradeoffs.

FinCrime & Identity Domain
  • Bring prior experience leading FinCrime/Fraud or Identity teams — understanding of typologies (card fraud, ATO, first-party fraud, synthetic identity, money mule networks), the regulatory context, and how detection strategy trades off against customer experience
  • Understand identity verification, KYC and onboarding data as a data domain, not just as a product surface
  • Partner with Risk, Compliance, and Legal on regulatory obligations tied to fraud and identity controls
  • Own incident response leadership when major fraud events, model failures, or data integrity failures occur
Bonus points
● Have worked at a scaling startup previously.
● Have experience with data mesh or domain-oriented data ownership models in practice, not just in theory.
● Have experience working with stablecoin and cryptocurrencies.
● Have experience working with AI in a production environment.
● Have worked in environments with k8s / gRPC / Spring Boot / Java / Python.

AI Literacy & Tools
As Zepz, we're building AI into how we work. We're on a journey to making AI utilisation streamline what we do. "For this position we are looking for:
  • Proficient depth of knowledge around automation, AI and how those can be applied in your area of work — from accelerating analysis and insight generation, to improving how we design and deliver processes and communications.
  • Practical experience using AI tools in a professional context — whether to connect information, draft content, build frameworks, or create insights from data. We want people who actively use AI to increase productivity, not those who are waiting to be told to.
  • Strong AI literacy — an understanding of what AI assistants can and cannot do, how to prompt effectively, and how to critically evaluate AI-generated output before using it.
  • Awareness of the ethical considerations and responsible use of AI in the workplace, particularly in the context of sensitive data, customer experience, and compliance.
  • Prior experience using Claude (Anthropic) is a nice-to-have but not essential — what matters most is that you are genuinely engaged with AI as a tool, comfortable experimenting, and eager to share what works with your wider team

If you want to join us in our journey to help break barriers in financial access and improve lives globally, there's no better place or time to join.

Our global team of 800+ people is spread across six continents. We aspire to hire the best mix of people from former Olympians to YouTube influencers and we speak over twenty languages. This incredible diversity isn't a bonus; it's the engine that lets us serve the world.

Ready to Apply? Let’s Go.

jobs.description:
Role: Jr. Product Manager, PreK-12
Team: Product
Reports to: VP, Product
Location: Flexible (Fully-Remote or Hybrid | Offices in NYC and Miami)

WHO WE ARE

The ASU+GSV Summit
Now in its 18th year, the ASU+GSV Summit is the world’s most important gathering of “PreK to Gray” education and workforce leaders. Held every April in San Diego, the 2026 event drew over 7,000 registrants to tackle the transformation of learning and skills delivery through generative AI, virtual reality, and other emerging technologies.

Frequently referred to as the “Davos of Education,” the ASU+GSV Summit brings together over 850 speakers each year, engaging in over 300 conversations around the future of learning and skills at scale. Past keynote speakers have included former President George W. Bush, Secretary Condoleezza Rice, Prime Minister Tony Blair, Sal Khan, Priscilla Chan, Ruby Bridges, Gloria Steinem, Jane Fonda, and countless others who have inspired our community to take bold action. Leading partners such as Google, Microsoft, Chan Zuckerberg Initiative, Gates Foundation, Walton Family Foundation, ClassDojo, and others help power this community. Through ongoing engagement and a global stage at ASU+GSV, you’ll help bring together the boldest thinkers reimagining what’s possible for the future of PreK-12 education.

As of July 2025, GSV Summit became part of Hyve Group's portfolio, joining forces with Bett to create the largest and most impactful education innovation community in the world, now reaching an audience of over 100,000 participants across five events on four continents.

WHO IS THE PRODUCT TEAM?

The Product Team is the creative and strategic engine behind the ASU+GSV Summit experience. We design and deliver the program of ASU+GSV, through curated content and experiences that inspire action: from high-production keynotes with global thought leaders to provocative panels, interactive workshops, community activations, and live product demos.

We bridge marketing, strategic partnerships, and community engagement to craft seamless, high-impact experiences for our attendees and partners. We collaborate closely with education leaders, practitioners, entrepreneurs, investors, policymakers, researchers, and thought leaders to shape the conversations that matter most in “PreK to Gray” learning.

Our work is structured around three core verticals—PreK-12, Higher Education, and Workforce—but the real power is in what we call “the magic in the mix.” Program often develops across verticals, so every team member takes a collaborative approach. We lean in to build the right program for the right audience at the right time, staying agile to launch new programs and rethink existing ones as needed.
ROLE OVERVIEW
We’re looking for a highly organized, execution-focused Jr. Product Manager to support the PreK-12 team at the ASU+GSV Summit. Reporting to the VP, Product and working closely with the Director, K12 Product, this role is about turning strategy into flawless execution. You will support in managing the details, logistics, and follow-through that bring the PreK-12 program to life.

Each year, 1,100+ PreK-12 leaders from 530+ districts and schools join us to explore the most pressing opportunities and challenges in PreK-12 education—from classroom innovation and educator support to school leadership, digital learning, and student outcomes.

You’ll partner closely with the Director, K12 Product to execute the PreK-12 content program, and collaborate with the SVP of Community, the VP of Educator Engagement, and the broader K12 community team to bring programming to life for our growing network of PreK-12 leaders. The role blends project management, program logistics, and cross-team coordination—requiring thoughtful collaboration, extreme precision, consistent follow-through, and a genuine curiosity about the PreK-12 landscape, including how AI is beginning to reshape it. That deep curiosity and eagerness to build understanding and discernment is what supports our team’s purpose: elevating the most cutting edge research, founders, and ideas, identifying the stars of tomorrow, and curating provocative conversations that push forward the most pressing challenges impacting the future of learning.


WHAT YOU WILL DO
As the Jr. Product Manager, PreK-12 you will be responsible for:

Program Execution & Project Management
  • Support the development and execution of the PreK-12 program under the direction of the Director, K12 Product—from researching emerging topics and identifying compelling voices to developing session concepts and bringing them to life at ASU+GSV Summit: ensuring that they are timely, relevant, and high-impact.
    • Across the product team, we work with 850+ speakers and 200+ partners to curate more 300 sessions each year, in addition to numerous bespoke community activations and experiences.
  • Supporting end-to-end program logistics: from speaker outreach and confirmation to session scheduling, run-of-show details, and final delivery.
  • Track and maintain accurate program documentation, session details, and speaker logistics with exceptional organization. No detail is too small.
  • Maintain the PreK-12 program calendar and pipeline, in coordination with partnership and community team to ensure a holistic approach, proactively flagging risks and dependencies

Partnership Support
  • Support the Director, K12 Product and the partnerships team in coordinating partner deliverables and activations tied to PreK-12 programming.
  • Track partner commitments and help ensure timely execution of partner-related program elements.
  • Help prepare materials and briefs for partner program involvement.
Community Collaboration
  • Partner closely with the SVP of Community, the VP of Educator Engagement, and the broader K12 community team to execute community engagement initiatives that support PreK-12 programming, in-person and year-round.
  • Help coordinate educator engagement touchpoints—webinars, community activations, and outreach—that feed the PreK-12 content pipeline.
  • Capture and organize community insights to help the Director, K12 Product surface emerging leaders, trends, and conversation topics.
Relationship Management & Stakeholder Communication
  • Serve as a day-to-day point of contact for PreK-12 speakers, moderators, and partners—managing logistics, scheduling, and communications with professionalism and responsiveness.
  • Support the Director, K12 Product in engaging PreK-12 superintendents, principals, educators, EdTech founders, and policymakers to inform program development and ensure content reflects the opportunities, challenges, and perspectives shaping the field.
Technology & Process Excellence
  • Use Airtable, Cvent, generative AI, and other tools to streamline workflows and enhance program delivery.
  • Identify and test new technologies that can improve efficiency, attendee experience, and business outcomes.

WHO YOU ARE
Experience
  • Bachelor’s degree
  • 1–2 years of previous experience in program/product management or a similar role that requires excellent attention to detail and ability to translate from strategy to execution
  • PreK-12 education or EdTech experience a strong plus

W Exclusive Networks pasjonujemy się wnoszeniem realnej różnicy. To oznacza dostarczanie najlepszych rozwiązań naszym klientom, wspieranie tworzenia bezpiecznego i zaufanego cyfrowego świata oraz pomoc naszym pracownikom w pełnym wykorzystaniu ich potencjału.

OBOWIĄZKI I ODPOWIEDZIALNOŚĆ | O roli

Będziesz odpowiedzialny za tworzenie, utrzymywanie i rozwijanie bezserwerowych oraz konteneryzowanych aplikacji krytycznych dla biznesu w JavaScript lub TypeScript.

Kluczowe aspekty opracowywanych rozwiązań to wydajność, skalowalność, możliwość testowania, niezawodność oraz przyszłościowa architektura. Twój wkład i zaangażowanie będą oczekiwane na każdym etapie procesu tworzenia oprogramowania.

Rola wymaga dobrej znajomości procesów biznesowych, ponieważ aplikacje zazwyczaj stanowią część większego rozwiązania obejmującego jedno lub więcej z poniższych: dostosowania ERP, RPA, AI, transformację danych, EDI, usługi internetowe i inne.

Stanowisko to obejmuje pracę zdalną w ramach globalnej organizacji, z okazjonalnymi podróżami w celu realizacji projektów lub współpracy z zespołami. Będziesz współpracować z właścicielami procesów biznesowych oraz zespołami IT przy tworzeniu i wdrażaniu rozwiązań. Będziesz raportować do Global Development Managera.

Jako Global Backend Developer będziesz:

  • Odpowiadać za tworzenie, utrzymywanie i rozwijanie bezserwerowych oraz konteneryzowanych aplikacji krytycznych dla biznesu w JavaScript lub TypeScript.
  • Współpracować z globalnymi zespołami IT i Development przy projektowaniu i wdrażaniu rozwiązań zgodnych z potrzebami biznesowymi.
  • Projektować, implementować i wdrażać wysoko skalowalne rozwiązania oparte na wymaganiach biznesowych.
  • Tworzyć plany testów, aby zapewnić zgodność rozwiązań z wymaganiami biznesowymi oraz wysokimi standardami jakości.
  • Współpracować z interesariuszami przy testach systemowych, testach akceptacyjnych użytkowników (UAT) oraz przeglądach po wdrożeniu.
  • Krok po kroku debugować rozwiązania w ramach wsparcia drugiej linii.

KWALIFIKACJE I DOŚWIADCZENIE | O Tobie

Idealny kandydat na stanowisko Global Backend Developer:

  • Posiada minimum 3–5 lat doświadczenia jako Back-End/Full-Stack JavaScript Developer w podobnym środowisku B2B.
  • Pisze czysty, kompletny, testowalny i dobrze udokumentowany kod.
  • Ma doświadczenie w tworzeniu rozproszonych aplikacji Node.js.
  • Zna i posiada praktyczną wiedzę na temat architektury opartej na zdarzeniach (Kafka, RabbitMQ, usługi chmurowe typu event bus).
  • Posługuje się językiem angielskim i jednym dodatkowym językiem europejskim (mile widziane).
  • Pracował w środowisku międzynarodowym.

KIM JESTEŚMY? | Dlaczego warto z nami pracować

Stawiamy na ludzi i mocno wierzymy, że talent pozwala nam kontynuować naszą historię innowacji i dalszego rozwoju w przyszłości. Naszą misją jest wspieranie przejścia do całkowicie zaufanego cyfrowego świata dla wszystkich ludzi i organizacji. Odwiedź naszą stronę .

Jesteśmy dumni, że jesteśmy Pracodawcą Równych Szans. Jesteśmy zaangażowani w rekrutację i zatrudnianie osób z różnych środowisk i doświadczeń, ponieważ wierzymy, że wzmacnia to naszą zdolność do opracowywania lepszych rozwiązań, podejmowania świadomych decyzji i lepszej obsługi naszych cenionych klientów. Nie dyskryminujemy osób ze względu na rasę, religię, kolor skóry, narodowość, płeć, orientację seksualną, niepełnosprawność czy jakąkolwiek podobną cechę. Decyzje dotyczące zatrudnienia podejmujemy wyłącznie na podstawie kwalifikacji, zasług i potrzeb biznesowych. Kliknij tutaj, aby zapoznać się z naszą Polityką Różnorodności i Integracji.
