The Role

Joining Moderna means advancing mRNA science to transform medicine. Work with exceptional global teams on a broad pipeline and build a career that makes a real difference for patients.

As Moderna expands its U.S. seasonal respiratory vaccine portfolio, we are seeking a strategic, transformational commercial leader to shape the future of regional account management, build high-performing teams, and accelerate vaccine adoption across complex healthcare systems. You will lead the evolution from broad, COVID-19-focused coverage to sophisticated, portfolio-based customer engagement, translating national commercial strategy into regional execution across COVID-19, influenza, RSV, and future launches. Through exceptional people leadership, strategic customer partnerships, and disciplined execution, you will connect enterprise-level access decisions with meaningful site-level activation and sustained portfolio growth.

This remote, field-based leadership opportunity will place you at the center of Moderna's evolving U.S. commercial model, with responsibility for leading Regional Account Managers (RAMs) across a defined U.S. region. You will drive strategic engagement with prioritized integrated delivery networks (IDNs), health systems, physician and provider networks, Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs), government and public-health customers, and relevant retail partners.

Here’s What You’ll Do

  • Lead and develop a high-performing regional account management team: Recruit, assess, onboard, coach, and retain exceptional Regional Account Managers, building the capabilities required for a more sophisticated, portfolio-focused commercial organization. Establish clear performance expectations and individualized development plans spanning strategic account planning, consultative selling, competitive positioning, contracting, customer engagement, and vaccine pull-through.
  • Translate national portfolio strategy into regional commercial impact: Develop and execute a disciplined regional account management strategy aligned with nationally established portfolio priorities and go-to-market objectives across COVID-19, influenza, RSV, and future launches. Adapt execution to distinct customer decision-makers, contracting calendars, competitive dynamics, and seasonal vaccine requirements while operating within established national strategy, contracting authorities, and compliance guardrails.
  • Build sophisticated, insight-driven strategic account plans: Lead the development, prioritization, and execution quality of comprehensive regional account plans informed by customer segmentation, portfolio opportunities, stakeholder mapping, purchasing behaviors, competitive intelligence, and account-specific objectives. Establish measurable milestones, clear accountability, and execution pathways that translate strategic opportunities into sustainable customer adoption.
  • Establish trusted partnerships with senior healthcare decision-makers: Build executive-level relationships across prioritized IDNs, health systems, provider networks, FQHCs, government and public-health organizations, and relevant retail partners. Represent Moderna in senior customer and public-health forums, strengthen the portfolio-level value proposition, and serve as a regional escalation and coordination leader for complex opportunities, ensuring clear ownership between Regional and National Account Management and functional partners.
  • Connect enterprise-level access to site-level vaccine adoption: Lead regional strategies that translate Group Purchasing Organization (GPO) arrangements, enterprise purchasing decisions, and health-system access opportunities into organizational opt-in, operational readiness, site-level activation, and sustained vaccine ordering and pull-through. Guide your team in navigating the interconnected clinical, economic, formulary, purchasing, and operational processes that influence adoption across complex healthcare systems.
  • Provide leadership across complex contracting and access pathways: Oversee account-level contracting readiness, escalation, and compliant execution in partnership with National Account Management, Market Access, Legal, Finance, and other authorized decision-makers. Equip RAMs to navigate GPO arrangements, health-system opt-in processes, formulary requirements, purchasing pathways, and implementation challenges while maintaining rigorous adherence to delegated contracting authorities and compliance requirements.
  • Develop engagement strategies across the complete healthcare stakeholder ecosystem: Coach your team to engage pharmacy leadership, population health, infectious disease, quality, ambulatory care, employee health, high-volume clinics, and other influential health-system stakeholders. Strengthen the team's ability to navigate clinical, economic, operational, and purchasing decision processes, bringing in Medical Affairs colleagues appropriately to support compliant scientific engagement.
  • Build a high-performance, change-ready leadership culture: Establish an environment defined by accountability, strong field coaching, capability assessment, performance calibration, and continuous improvement. Reinforce manager-led coaching practices and consistently evaluate both the quality of strategic customer engagement and the delivery of measurable business outcomes, supporting the team through evolving commercial priorities and operating models.
  • Shape the future of regional account management capabilities: Partner closely with Field Enablement & Capabilities to translate enterprise standards into consistent hiring criteria, onboarding experiences, training adoption, coaching frameworks, and readiness assessments. Identify critical capability gaps and develop targeted interventions that prepare RAMs for increasingly complex portfolio-based engagement, competitive positioning, and customer activation.
  • Turn customer and market intelligence into strategic advantage: Systematically synthesize insights from regional field engagement, customer decision-making, competitive activity, purchasing behavior, and evolving healthcare market dynamics. Translate these insights into sharper account prioritization, portfolio positioning, regional resource deployment, national commercial planning, and continuous refinement of Moderna's go-to-market model.
  • Drive performance through advanced analytics and digital tools: Leverage CRM platforms, strategic account planning tools, field analytics, and established leading and lagging performance indicators to assess target-account coverage, stakeholder engagement, account-plan progression, contract activation, ordering patterns, customer adoption, and regional business results. Identify data-quality gaps, challenge assumptions, and adjust resource deployment and engagement strategies based on actionable insights. Explore opportunities to apply digital innovation, including emerging Generative AI-enabled tools where approved, to enhance account insights, coaching effectiveness, and commercial productivity.
  • Establish a balanced approach to commercial performance management: Monitor regional outcomes, including vaccine volume, market share, and customer adoption, alongside leading indicators such as priority-account engagement, decision-maker coverage, strategic account-plan progress, and implementation milestones. Use these measures to strengthen execution discipline, identify barriers early, and drive consistent improvement in both near-term results and long-term account development.
  • Orchestrate seamless cross-functional commercial execution: Work collaboratively with National Account Management, Medical Affairs, Marketing, Market Access, Public Affairs, Commercial Excellence, Distribution, Customer Service, and approved external channel partners to deliver coordinated customer engagement. Clarify account ownership, functional responsibilities, escalation pathways, and execution priorities while maintaining appropriate boundaries between promotional activity and scientific exchange.
  • Lead transformational change across the regional commercial model: Guide your team through a multi-year evolution from broad, COVID-19-oriented coverage toward targeted, sophisticated, portfolio-based account engagement. Champion new deployment approaches, strengthen team readiness, preserve customer continuity, and clarify ownership across regional and national teams. Capture learnings from commercial pilots and emerging go-to-market channels to support scalable improvements across the organization.
  • Strengthen regional execution through customer activation and operational excellence: Connect regional account strategies with practical implementation requirements across health systems, provider networks, public-health customers, and relevant retail partners. Coordinate with internal and external stakeholders to resolve implementation barriers, strengthen contracting-to-activation processes, and ensure customer decisions translate into consistent site-level adoption and sustained vaccine access.
  • Champion integrity, accountability, and compliant customer engagement: Ensure all regional account management activities comply with Moderna policies and applicable healthcare laws and regulations. Maintain appropriate separation between promotional and scientific exchange, ensure adherence to approved product labeling, and reinforce disciplined decision-making within established contracting authorities and organizational compliance standards.

Blink Health is a healthcare technology company that builds products to make prescriptions accessible and affordable to everybody. You will report directly to the VP of Customer Growth and work as a core member of a small, nimble team of marketers, engineers, and product managers who move fast and have real influence over how millions of patients access their medications. You will have a front-row seat to modern AI-enabled marketing at scale, with the ability to experiment, ship, and see impact quickly. This role sits within a globally distributed team, which means you will collaborate closely with US-based counterparts and leadership, including regular evening availability to align across time zones.

About the Role

Blink is seeking a strategic, hands-on Online Marketing Manager Growth & Lifecycle Marketing Manager to lead omnichannel lifecycle and performance marketing programs that improve patient outcomes and accelerate business growth. This role will own strategy, execution, and optimization across email, SMS, push, in-app, voice, paid search, paid social, display, and emerging digital channels. The ideal candidate blends strong marketing fundamentals with analytical rigor and practical use of AI to improve personalization, segmentation, creative velocity, and operational efficiency. You will work cross-functionally with sales, client development, product, analytics, data science, engineering, and compliance to deliver measurable impact while maintaining a high bar for patient experience, privacy, and brand integrity. This is a globally distributed team. You will work closely with US-based leadership and peers and should be comfortable with regular evening availability to support real-time collaboration across time zones.

Responsibilities

  • Develop and lead an integrated online marketing and lifecycle strategy that supports patient outcomes while driving acquisition, activation, retention, adherence, and re-engagement goals.
  • Own CRM and lifecycle programs across email, SMS, push, in-app messaging, and voice, including journey design, trigger strategy, audience selection, content planning, and performance optimization.
  • Apply AI-enabled approaches to audience segmentation, personalization, send-time optimization, churn-risk identification, propensity modeling, and next-best-action recommendations.
  • Partner with data science and analytics to operationalize predictive models and evaluate whether AI-driven interventions improve engagement, conversion, refill behavior, retention, lifetime value, and ROI.
  • Design and execute a rigorous experimentation roadmap across lifecycle and paid channels, including A/B, holdout, and multivariate tests; measure incrementality and causal impact wherever possible.
  • Lead paid digital marketing efforts across SEM, PLA or shopping, paid social, display, retargeting, and partner channels, optimizing toward CAC, ROAS, conversion rate, and long-term value.
  • Own marketing measurement frameworks, attribution methodologies, and executive reporting; translate campaign and channel performance into actionable recommendations for leadership.
  • Improve campaign development workflows through AI-assisted copy ideation, creative testing, QA support, and audience operations, with human review and clear brand and compliance guardrails.
  • Collaborate with product and engineering to improve martech infrastructure, conversion tracking, event instrumentation, data quality, and campaign orchestration across the patient journey.
  • Build and maintain scalable segmentation logic and first-party data strategies within CRM, CDP, and analytics environments to increase relevance and efficiency across channels.
  • Ensure responsible use of AI and patient data in partnership with legal and compliance teams, with attention to privacy, consent, bias mitigation, explainability, and healthcare marketing requirements. Partner with legal and compliance teams to ensure AI tools and patient data are used responsibly, with attention to privacy, consent, and bias mitigation. You will have guardrails and support, not sole ownership of this domain.
  • Stay current on digital marketing trends, platform changes, privacy shifts, healthcare engagement best practices, and emerging AI capabilities; translate relevant developments into pragmatic pilots and scaled programs.
  • Mentor junior team members and agency partners, and help raise the team standard for testing discipline, measurement rigor, and modern marketing operations.

Qualifications

  • 5+ years of experience in online, lifecycle, CRM, growth, or performance marketing, with meaningful ownership of patient or customer engagement programs.
  • Bachelor's degree in marketing, statistics, business, communications, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Demonstrated experience working with or within US-based companies, including comfort navigating US business culture, cross-timezone collaboration, and US consumer marketing standards.
  • Demonstrated success managing omnichannel campaigns across owned and paid channels, with accountability for measurable business outcomes.
  • Hands-on experience applying AI, automation, predictive analytics, or generative AI tools to marketing workflows, audience strategy, experimentation, or content operations.
  • Strong AI aptitude, including curiosity, sound judgment, and practical experience using AI tools to accelerate research, content development, campaign optimization, analysis, and day-to-day marketing workflows.
  • Strong analytical and technical skills, including expertise in SQL and experience with BI and visualization tools such as Tableau, Looker, or similar platforms.
  • Experience with CRM and marketing automation platforms such as Braze, Iterable, Salesforce Marketing Cloud, or similar tools.
  • Experience with digital advertising platforms such as Google Ads, Meta, paid social, display, and retargeting platforms.
  • Deep understanding of segmentation, funnel analysis, attribution, incrementality measurement, and test design.
  • Excellent project management and cross-functional collaboration skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-moving environment.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Self-starter with a strong work ethic and a track record of delivering results while working with distributed or remote teams.
  • Comfortable with regular evening availability to collaborate with US-based team members and leadership in real time.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in healthcare technology, digital health, pharmacy, or another regulated consumer industry.
  • Experience partnering with data science, product, and engineering teams to bring new measurement, modeling, or personalization capabilities into production.
  • Familiarity with CDPs, data warehousing, reverse ETL, or modern marketing data stacks.
  • Experience evaluating AI vendors, prompts, copilots, or marketing automation tools for quality, risk, and business impact.
  • MBA or other advanced degree is a plus. MBA strongly preferred.

If you are a strategic marketer with strong analytical instincts and a practical approach to AI-enabled growth, we encourage you to apply. If you are a curious, fast-moving marketer who thrives in a high-ownership environment, is energized by AI-enabled growth, and wants to do your best work on a global team, we would love to hear from you.

Why Join Us:It is rare to have a company that both deeply impacts its customers and is able to provide its services across a massive population. At Blink, we have a huge impact on people when they are most vulnerable: at the intersection of their healthcare and finances. We are also the fastest growing healthcare company in the country and are driving that impact across millions of new patients every year. Our business model not only helps people, but drives economics that allow us to build a generational company. We are a relentlessly learning, constantly curious, and aggressively collaborative cross-functional team dedicated to inventing new ways to improve the lives of our customers.

About the Role:

Grade Level (for internal use):

12

The Role

S&P Dow Jones Indices is seeking a commercially minded Associate Director, Multi-Asset Product Management to join our Multi-Asset Product Management team in New York.


This role will support the development and growth of S&P DJI's multi-asset index franchise across a broad range of index-linked investment solutions, including defined outcome, risk-controlled, asset allocation, retirement, insurance, structured product, and derivatives-based strategies.


The ideal candidate will bring a strong background in multi-asset product management or investment solutions, experience supporting product development initiatives, and a solid understanding of systematic investment strategies. While familiarity with options and derivatives is valuable, success in this role will be driven by the ability to manage products across their lifecycle, understand client needs, and translate investment concepts into commercially relevant solutions.


This role requires close partnership with clients, Sales, Research & Design, Index Governance, Marketing, Technology, and other stakeholders. The successful candidate will combine technical knowledge, commercial awareness, strong communication skills, and the ability to work effectively across a global matrixed organization.


The Team

The Multi-Asset Product Management team at S&P Dow Jones Indices is responsible for setting product strategy, driving product development, and managing the long-term commercial success of a global suite of multi-asset indices.


The team develops solutions for a broad range of client segments, including banks, asset managers, ETF issuers, insurance companies, wealth platforms, and institutional investors. The product suite includes strategies focused on index-linked insurance products, structured products, derivatives overlays, volatility control, retirement solutions, asset allocation, and other systematic multi-asset strategies.


The team has a global mandate and works closely with regional commercial teams and clients to identify market opportunities, launch innovative index solutions, and support adoption of S&P DJI’s multi-asset capabilities.


Responsibilities and Impact

  • Support the research, development, and launch of systematic multi-asset indices and investment solutions, including asset allocation, risk-controlled, target outcome, insurance-related, and derivatives-based strategies, partnering with Research & Design and Index Governance to establish transparent, rules-based methodologies.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally across Product Management, Research & Design, Index Governance, Sales, Marketing, Legal, Compliance, Operations, and Technology to drive product outcomes without direct management authority.
  • Serve as a subject matter expert in client meetings, product pitches, trainings, and conferences, translating complex index strategies into clear commercial narratives and client solutions.
  • Contribute to thought leadership and product positioning through presentations, white papers, client materials, market commentary, and internal and external product messaging.
  • Monitor market trends, client needs, and the competitive landscape — including QIS desks, investment banks, exchanges, structured product platforms, ETF issuers, and insurance providers — to identify new product opportunities and inform product strategy.
  • Support the lifecycle management of the existing multi-asset index suite, tracking product performance, commercial traction, and market relevance to identify opportunities for enhancements and repositioning.

What’s In It For You

  • The opportunity to contribute to product strategy and innovation for a sophisticated and commercially important global index product suite.
  • Direct involvement in developing multi-asset index solutions used across ETFs, retirement products, insurance solutions, structured products, and institutional investment applications.
  • Regular interaction with clients, commercial teams, quantitative researchers, index governance stakeholders, and product leaders across S&P Dow Jones Indices.
  • The opportunity to build deep expertise across multi-asset and systematic investment strategies while contributing to an area of growing client demand.
  • A role combining product development, investment expertise, client engagement, and commercial execution.

Compensation/Benefits Information (US Applicants Only)

S&P Global states that the anticipated base salary range for this position is $104-435 – $170,1470. Final base salary for this role will be based on the individual’s geographic location, as well as experience level, skill set, training, licenses, and certifications.

In addition to base compensation, this role is eligible for an annual incentive plan. This role is eligible to receive additional S&P Global benefits.


What We’re Looking For

We are looking for an experienced product management or investment professional with a strong understanding of multi-asset investment solutions and experience supporting product development, strategy, and commercialization.


The successful candidate will possess knowledge of systematic investment approaches, including asset allocation, target outcome, risk-controlled, retirement, insurance, and derivatives-linked strategies, and will be comfortable operating at the intersection of product development, client engagement, and commercial execution.


Experience supporting investment solutions designed to address client objectives such as income generation, risk management, volatility control, capital preservation, participation enhancement, and retirement outcomes is highly desirable. Familiarity with options and derivatives-based approaches is beneficial but is not required to have been a primary area of specialization.


This individual should be comfortable discussing methodology and investment concepts with quantitative stakeholders while also articulating the commercial value proposition to clients and sales teams.


Basic Required Qualifications

  • 7+ years of experience in product management, index strategy, investment solutions, asset management, or related financial services roles, with demonstrable exposure to multi-asset investment strategies.
  • Quantitative background with an understanding of index construction, portfolio design, and multi-asset investment strategies, including asset allocation, retirement, target outcome, risk-controlled, insurance-linked, and derivatives-based approaches.
  • Proven ability to influence cross-functional stakeholders across Product, Research & Design, Sales, Governance, Marketing, Operations, and Technology, and to drive outcomes collaboratively.
  • Commercial mindset with demonstrated experience supporting product adoption, client engagement, and revenue growth for investment, index, or multi-asset solutions.
  • Bachelor's degree in Finance, Mathematics, Economics, Statistics, Engineering, or Computer Science.

Additional Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience supporting or developing multi-asset index solutions, including target outcome, risk-controlled, retirement, insurance-linked, volatility-controlled, or derivatives-linked strategies.
  • Familiarity with index methodology governance, launch lifecycle, and operational considerations for investable indices.
  • Advanced degree and/or professional credentials (e.g., CFA, CAIA) and/or programming skills (Python, R, or MATLAB).
  • Experience building models, backtests, simulations, risk analytics, or index strategy prototypes.
  • Experience presenting at client meetings, conferences, webinars, or sales training forums.
  • Strong understanding of the competitive landscape across QIS desks, investment banks, exchanges, index providers, ETF issuers, and structured product platforms.
  • Experience mentoring or developing junior product management professionals.

Right to Work Requirements: This role is limited to persons with indefinite right to work in the United States.

At S&P Dow Jones Indices, we provide iconic and innovative index solutions backed by unparalleled expertise across the asset-class spectrum. By bringing transparency to the global capital markets, we empower investors everywhere to make decisions with conviction. We’re the largest global resource for index-based concepts, data and research, and home to iconic financial market indicators, such as the S&P 500® and the Dow Jones Industrial Average®. About GlobalFoundries:

GlobalFoundries is a leading full-service semiconductor foundry providing a unique combination of design, development, and fabrication services to some of the world’s most inspired technology companies. Summary of Role:

GlobalFoundries is seeking a Senior Analog Design Engineer to develop advanced analog and mixed-signal integrated circuits and reusable IP for emerging semiconductor applications, including cryogenic CMOS and quantum systems. This role will drive designs from circuit architecture through tapeout and silicon validation while partnering closely with technology, PDK, modeling, and test teams.


Essential Responsibilities:

  • Design and develop high-performance analog and mixed-signal CMOS circuits and reusable IP, including amplifiers, bias and reference circuits, regulators, data converters, oscillators, PLLs, clocking circuits, and drivers.
  • Own circuit development from architecture and transistor-level design through simulation, layout supervision, physical verification, tapeout, silicon characterization, and design-to-measurement correlation.
  • Perform comprehensive circuit analysis across process, voltage, and temperature, including Monte Carlo/mismatch, noise, stability, linearity, timing, and post-layout parasitic simulations.
  • Optimize circuit performance across operating temperature ranges, including cryogenic conditions, power constraints, process variation, device behavior, and layout-dependent effects.
  • Collaborate with device modeling and PDK teams to assess model accuracy, identify model or design-rule gaps, and provide circuit-level feedback supporting cryogenic and advanced PDK development and validation.
  • Drive analog layout requirements and reviews for device matching, common-centroid structures, shielding, isolation, parasitic management, signal integrity, power integrity, and design for manufacturability.
  • Define silicon test structures and characterization plans, analyze measured data, debug performance issues, and correlate hardware results with pre-silicon simulation and compact models.
  • Lead technical design reviews, document design methodology and results, mentor engineers, and collaborate with cross-functional internal and external teams to enable customer and technology solutions.

Other Responsibilities:

  • Perform all activities in a safe and responsible manner and support all Environmental, Health, Safety & Security requirements and programs.

Required Qualifications:

  • Education - Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Microelectronics, Computer Engineering, Applied Physics, or a related field.
  • Experience - Minimum 5 years of relevant analog or mixed-signal integrated circuit design experience.
  • Skills - Demonstrated experience taking analog or mixed-signal circuits through schematic design, simulation, layout, DRC/LVS, parasitic extraction, tapeout, and silicon validation.
  • Skills - Strong knowledge of CMOS analog design fundamentals, including device physics, noise, matching, feedback, stability, frequency response, process variation, and PVT/Monte Carlo analysis.
  • Skills - Proficiency with industry-standard analog IC design, SPICE simulation, layout, physical verification, and post-layout extraction environments.
  • Skills - Ability to independently analyze complex circuit and silicon performance issues and translate results into design improvements.

• Travel - Up to 10%.

  • Fluency in English Language - written & verbal.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Education - Master’s degree or PhD in Electrical Engineering, Microelectronics, or a related field.
  • Experience - Experience with cryogenic CMOS, low-temperature circuit design or characterization, quantum-control electronics, precision instrumentation, RF, or other advanced analog applications.
  • Skills - Familiarity with CMOS device behavior and compact-model limitations at cryogenic temperatures.
  • Skills - Experience designing advanced analog/mixed-signal blocks such as ADCs/DACs, PLLs, LNAs, VGAs, oscillators, voltage/current references, LDOs, or high-speed drivers.
  • Skills - Experience with silicon characterization and correlation of measured results to simulation, including interactions with device modeling, PDK, process technology, or test teams.
  • Skills - Familiarity with design or characterization automation using Python, SKILL, Tcl, or equivalent scripting languages.

About Us

We are a global climate technologies company engineered for sustainability. We create sustainable and efficient residential, commercial and industrial spaces through HVACR technologies. Job Summary

We are seeking an experienced Firmware Engineering Manager to lead our embedded systems team with a dedicated focus on technical execution and regulatory alignment under the EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA). In this role, you will lead a team of firmware engineers owning existing and new secure, scalable IoT products while ensuring our entire embedded architecture and software development lifecycle (SDLC) meet mandatory EU cybersecurity requirements.


You will bridge the gap between low-level firmware development, security architecture, and regulatory compliance—ensuring our devices are secure by design, maintain continuous vulnerability management, and support robust over-the-air (OTA) updates throughout their support lifecycle.


Key Responsibilities

Technical Leadership & CRA Implementation

  • Secure Architecture: Drive the design and implementation of firmware security controls aligned with CRA standards (e.g., ETSI EN 303 645, IEC 62443, ISO 27001), enforcing Hardware Root of Trust, Secure Boot, encrypted memory partitions, and secure key storage.
  • Automated SBOM & Dependency Management: Establish automated generation and maintenance of Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) (e.g., CycloneDX, SPDX) within build pipelines to maintain component transparency and track open-source dependencies.
  • Over-the-Air (OTA) & Patch Management: Direct the development of secure, cryptographically signed, and resilient OTA update mechanisms capable of delivering rapid security patches without bricking devices in the field.
  • Vulnerability & Incident Management: Implement processes to meet CRA reporting mandates—including 24-hour initial vulnerability alert capabilities, 72-hour notifications, and rapid patch deployment workflows.
  • Conformity & Technical Documentation: Oversee technical file generation, risk assessments, and compliance testing required for CRA CE marking and third-party conformity audits.

People & Team Management

  • Lead, mentor, and grow a team of embedded firmware engineers, fostering a culture prioritizing security-by-design and security-by-default principles.
  • Balance feature delivery roadmaps with compliance deadlines, security debt reduction, and refactoring efforts.
  • Conduct code reviews, establish secure coding standards (MISRA, CERT C), and integrate SAST/DAST/fuzz testing tools into CI/CD build environments.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Partner closely with Product Management, Hardware Design, Legal/Compliance, and Cloud IoT teams to align hardware selection (e.g., Secure Elements, TPMs) with security standards.
  • Serve as the technical point of contact for external auditors, compliance bodies, and security researchers conducting vulnerability assessments or penetration testing.

Required Qualifications

  • Education: Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Experience:
    • 8+ years of experience in embedded firmware development (C/C++, RTOS, bare-metal, or Embedded Linux), preferably for IoT devices.
    • 3+ years of experience in an engineering management, tech lead, or supervisory role.
    • Demonstrated experience implementing firmware security primitives: Secure Boot, cryptographic hardware (HSM, TPM, Secure Elements), TLS/mTLS, memory protection, and secure storage.
    • Authorization to work in the United States - sponsorship will not be provided for this role. Temporary visas such as F1 (OPT & STEM), H1, L, B, J, or TN are not eligible.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Hands-on knowledge of hardware/software security frameworks and regulatory compliance standards (e.g., EU Cyber Resilience Act, ETSI EN 303 645, NIST SP 800-213, IEC 62443).
  • Experience establishing automated SBOM pipelines and vulnerability scanning (e.g., CVE mapping).
  • Deep experience with microcontroller architectures (ARM Cortex-M/TrustZone, RISC-V, ESP32) and wireless protocols (BLE, Wi-Fi, Cellular IoT, Thread/Matter).
  • Knowledge of global IoT cybersecurity legislation beyond the EU (e.g., US Cyber Trust Mark, UK PSTI Act).
  • Active cybersecurity certification (e.g., CISSP, CSSLP, or CISM).

Pay Transparency: $95,500 - $171,900 USD Annually

Across the globe, we are united by a singular Purpose: Sustainability is no small ambition. That’s why everything we do is geared toward a sustainable future—for our generation and all those to come. As the Health Segment Finance Lead, you are the Chief Financial Officer for Guidehouse’s largest segment and the nexus between Segment leadership and Corporate Finance.   • Lead the Segment’s and practice areas’ annual planning and quarterly forecasting activities:
    • Collaborate with Project Finance Delivery / Project Controls, Segment leadership, and practice leaders to set targets and build up revenue, margin, headcount, and key drivers—grounded in contract-level realities, delivery capacity, and observed performance trends.

  • Ability to independently explain results, variances, and forward outlook at both aggregate and underlying driver levels—leveraging strong Excel/modeling and data-wrangling skills to translate complex data into succinct, decision-ready insight.

Overview

Systems Planning and Analysis, Inc. (SPA) delivers high-impact, technical solutions to complex national security issues. With over 50 years of business expertise and consistent growth, we are known for continuous innovation for our government customers, in both the US and abroad. Our exceptionally talented team is highly collaborative in spirit and practice, producing Results that Matter. Come work with the best! The Space and Intelligence Division provides professional services to the US Space Force, Combatant Commands, Intelligence Community, and NASA. Our work includes enterprise architectural assessments, systems engineering and integration, test, planning and execution, cost estimating and analysis, acquisition support, and cybersecurity. We are trusted partners developing approaches and concepts to meet emerging high priority needs, assessing cutting-edge technologies, and supporting capabilities for our National Defense. Come join the fastest growing Division at Systems Planning and Analysis, Inc.!

The Space Systems Group (SSG), part of SPA’s Space and Intelligence Division, provides timely and objective assessments and recommendations integrating technical, operational, programmatic, policy and business analysis. We focus on our key clients in the Space community including the US Space Force’s Space Systems Command (USSF/SSC), one of the three designated Field Commands under USSF. We work tirelessly to provide integrated solutions based on information and communications throughout the chain of command. We provide clear and consistent analysis and recommendations which are aligned to strategic and leadership goals while balancing the ability to execute on time and on budget within the technical communities. Come join an organization responsible for being a key enabler of Spacepower!


Responsibilities

SPA has a need for a Senior Data Platform Engineer to design, implement, operate, and optimize modern data platforms supporting mission-critical enterprise applications and services.

The ideal candidate combines the foundational expertise of a Database Administrator (DBA) with the engineering capabilities of a cloud-native platform specialist and the architectural understanding of modern distributed data systems.

This position extends well beyond traditional database administration or SQL-centric data engineering. The successful candidate will have practical experience across relational and non-relational databases, managed cloud database services, event-driven architectures, streaming platforms, data processing frameworks, and analytical data systems. The engineer will work closely with platform engineering, software development, cybersecurity, and systems architecture teams to deliver scalable, secure, highly available, and operationally sustainable data capabilities across hybrid and multi-cloud environments.

Key Responsibilities

Database Engineering and Administration

  • Design, deploy, configure, maintain, and optimize enterprise relational and non-relational database systems.
  • Provide advanced database administration expertise, including performance tuning, query optimization, indexing, replication, backup and recovery, and capacity planning.
  • Engineer high-availability and disaster recovery solutions, including clustering, automated failover, point-in-time recovery, and cross-region replication.
  • Support database lifecycle management, including version upgrades, schema migrations, patching, and operational automation.
  • Establish database security standards covering encryption, access controls, auditing, credential management, and data protection.
  • Troubleshoot complex database performance, availability, and consistency issues across distributed environments.

Cloud-Native and Managed Data Services

  • Architect, deploy, and operate data services within Kubernetes and cloud-native environments.
  • Implement and manage database platforms using Kubernetes operators, Helm, GitOps, and Infrastructure as Code (IaC).
  • Engineer solutions using managed cloud database offerings such as Azure Database for PostgreSQL, Azure SQL, Amazon RDS/Aurora, or equivalent services.
  • Evaluate tradeoffs between self-managed, Kubernetes-hosted, and cloud-managed database offerings based on operational complexity, performance, resilience, security, and cost.
  • Implement automation for provisioning, scaling, configuration management, observability, backup, and recovery.
  • Integrate data services with enterprise identity, secrets management, networking, and security platforms.

Distributed Data and Streaming Engineering

  • Design and implement distributed, event-driven data architectures supporting asynchronous messaging, event ingestion, and near-real-time processing.
  • Engineer and maintain streaming and messaging platforms such as Apache Kafka, NATS, or equivalent technologies.
  • Develop and maintain data ingestion, transformation, routing, and integration pipelines across heterogeneous systems.
  • Apply distributed systems concepts including message delivery semantics, ordering, replay, idempotency, partitioning, and fault tolerance.
  • Implement schema governance, serialization, and data contract management using technologies such as Avro, Protobuf, JSON Schema, and schema registries.
  • Design reliable data movement and replication strategies across clusters, regions, and environments.

Data Processing, Analytics, and Storage

  • Design and support batch and streaming data processing solutions using frameworks such as Apache Spark, Flink, or equivalent technologies.
  • Work with data lakes, lakehouse architectures, object storage, analytical databases, and distributed query engines.
  • Engineer data ingestion and transformation workflows supporting structured, semi-structured, and unstructured data.
  • Support analytical and operational workloads with appropriate data modeling, partitioning, indexing, lifecycle management, and storage optimization.
  • Evaluate and integrate technologies such as Trino, ClickHouse, Apache Iceberg, Delta Lake, or equivalent solutions.
  • Implement data quality, validation, lineage, metadata management, and governance capabilities.

Platform Reliability, Security, and Automation

  • Develop infrastructure automation and GitOps workflows using Terraform, OpenTofu, Ansible, Argo CD, or equivalent technologies.
  • Build production-ready data platforms with appropriate monitoring, alerting, logging, and performance telemetry.
  • Establish service-level objectives, resilience requirements, recovery objectives, and operational runbooks.
  • Collaborate with cybersecurity teams to implement data protection, encryption, identity integration, and compliance controls.
  • Participate in architecture reviews, technical evaluations, incident resolution, and root cause analysis.
  • Mentor engineers and contribute to technical standards, reference architectures, and engineering best practices.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

  • US Citizenship + Secret clearance at date of application
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Information Systems, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent relevant professional experience
  • 7+ years of relevant experience in database administration, data engineering, platform engineering, or distributed data systems
  • Demonstrated hands-on expertise administering and optimizing production relational databases, preferably PostgreSQL, including replication, backup/recovery, performance tuning, and high availability
  • Working knowledge of non-relational data stores, including document, key-value, or other NoSQL database technologies
  • Production experience with at least one major cloud provider, preferably Microsoft Azure, including managed database services
  • Hands-on experience with Kubernetes, containerized workloads, and cloud-native deployment patterns
  • Practical experience with event streaming or distributed messaging technologies, preferably Apache Kafka or NATS
  • Experience building or supporting ETL/ELT pipelines, data integration workflows, or distributed data processing systems
  • Working knowledge of data lakes, analytical storage architectures, and modern data processing technologies
  • Strong proficiency in SQL and at least one general-purpose programming or scripting language such as Python, Go, or Java
  • Experience with automation, Infrastructure as Code, CI/CD, and version-controlled infrastructure configurations
  • Strong understanding of distributed systems fundamentals, networking, security, storage, and fault tolerance
  • Demonstrated ability to independently troubleshoot complex production issues spanning application, database, infrastructure, and network layers

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server, Azure SQL, Azure Storage, or other Azure-native data services
  • Experience operating PostgreSQL on Kubernetes using CloudNativePG, Crunchy Postgres, or similar operators
  • Expertise in PostgreSQL clustering technologies such as Patroni, etcd-based coordination, or equivalent high-availability solutions

Elements of the compensation package include competitive base pay and variable compensation opportunities. Job Description

A bit more about this role:

This is an exciting opportunity for a compassionate and skilled Advanced Practice Provider (APRN or PA) to provide virtual primary care to a panel of patients through our innovative telehealth platform. As a Primary Care Advanced Practice Provider (Longitudinal Chronic Disease Management), you’ll manage that panel of patients on their primary care journey with Devoted Medical. You’ll conduct comprehensive clinical assessments, develop plans for chronic condition management, and work on preventative and proactive care. You’ll collaborate closely with specialists, pharmacists, nurses, care coordinators, caregivers, and families to deliver coordinated, member-centered care.

You will also provide that panel with ongoing management of their new and chronic conditions, preventive screenings, and medication management, all through a virtual care model. You'll work collaboratively with a multidisciplinary team to coordinate in-person services such as lab work, imaging, and specialist referrals as needed. You’ll partner with our Physician team on more complex patients.

We’re not just looking for a provider—we’re looking for a healthcare innovator who embraces change, values patient-centered care, and is excited about making healthcare better through compassion supported with technology.

Responsibilities will include:

  • Deliver longitudinal virtual primary care visits via telehealth to a panel of patients.

  • Be the anchor to an interdisciplinary primary care team, leveraging urgent care, specialty, digital teams to deliver access and quality care

  • Diagnose and manage chronic conditions (e.g., hypertension, diabetes, COPD, heart disease, etc.) and develop individualized care plans to optimize patient health.

  • Order and interpret lab tests, imaging, and other diagnostics, coordinating follow-up care as necessary.

  • Manage medication prescriptions including controlled substances, titrations, and refills, ensuring patient adherence and safety.

  • Provide health coaching, lifestyle modification guidance, and patient education to empower patients in managing their health.

  • Identify patients needing referrals, or home-based services, and facilitate appropriate coordination with specialists or community resources.

  • Utilize and provide feedback on our electronic health platform, contributing to its continuous improvement to enhance patient and provider experience.

  • Participate in clinical case reviews, team huddles, and interdisciplinary collaborations to ensure high-quality, patient-centered care.

  • Engage in continuous learning and improvement, staying up-to-date with best practices in virtual care and primary care management.

Attributes to success:

  • Patient-centered & compassionate – You put patients first, ensuring they feel heard, supported, and empowered in their health journey.

  • Skilled in primary care & chronic disease management – You have deep knowledge of treating and managing common conditions in adult and geriatric populations.

  • Tech-savvy & adaptable – You’re comfortable using electronic health records, telehealth platforms, and digital tools to enhance care.

  • Collaborative & team-oriented – You work well with other clinicians, care coordinators, and administrative staff to provide integrated care.

  • Proactive & problem-solving mindset – You identify challenges in healthcare delivery and actively contribute to solutions.

  • Strong communicator – You can explain medical concepts clearly to patients, families, and team members in a virtual environment.

jobs.excerpt: About WhiteMatter WhiteMatter is the first agent-native company that secures and operationalizes the agentic enterprise across the entire agent lifecycle.
jobs.description:
About WhiteMatter

WhiteMatter is the first agent-native company that secures and operationalizes the agentic enterprise across the entire agent lifecycle. Foundation models are non-deterministic, so protecting agents only at runtime leaves every decision to the last millisecond and every alert to the security team. WhiteMatter treats AI as a deployment problem first: every agent is assessed, governed against policy, and deployed from an approved blueprint before it reaches production; every action it takes is decided before it executes; and every outcome is proven after it runs. Founded by security veterans and deployed across, WhiteMatter is headquartered in Austin, Texas. Make every agent matter.

Why Join Us

We are building the infrastructure that makes safe, autonomous AI a reality for the enterprise. Joining our team means tackling unsolved engineering and security challenges at the absolute cutting edge of agentic AI. We operate with high velocity, value ownership, and are backed by top-tier investors. If you want to shape how the world's most advanced AI systems are governed and deployed, we want you on board.

About the Role

The Sales Engineer is the technical authority and narrative driver in customer engagements. This role is responsible for translating complex AI, Identity, and Data Protection challenges into defensible, real-world solutions—while helping customers understand not just how something works, but why it matters. This role blends deep hands-on technical expertise with storytelling, big-picture (“paint the picture”) thinking, and collaborative problem solving. You will work with prospects to obtain the technical win by designing a viable technical solution with an amazing product that can be applied to various scenarios. You will operate across AI security, LLMs, AI agents, MCP, DLP, and Identity, partnering closely with Sales, Product, and Engineering to close deals and influence product direction.

Key Responsibilities

Technical Discovery & Storytelling

  • Lead technical discovery for AI security, DLP, and Identity-driven use cases.
  • Translate complex security architectures into clear narratives that resonate with:

○ CISOs and VP’s

○ Security leaders

○ Architects

○ Engineers

○ Business stakeholders

  • “Paint the big picture” by connecting AI usage, identity trust, and data protection into a cohesive story.
  • Clearly articulate what problems are solvable today, what are partially solvable, and what are structural limitations.

Architecture & Solution Design

  • Design and present end-to-end architectures covering:

○ LLM and AI agent workflows (human + non-human identities)

○ Data protection, inspection, and policy enforcement

○ Identity, authentication, authorization, and trust boundaries

  • Build, configure, and run demos and POCs using Dockerized components.
  • Integrate enterprise environments including:

○ Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD), Okta

○ Microsoft Intune, Jamf Pro

  • Explain and demonstrate AI pipelines using:

○ LangChain, LangGraph

○ MCP-style agent orchestration patterns

  • Lead deep dives into DLP architectures, including:

○ What DLP can realistically detect and enforce

○ Where traditional DLP breaks down (AI, agents, encrypted channels, context loss)

○ Common false assumptions customers have about DLP coverage

  • Help customers understand enforcement gaps, bypass scenarios, and risk trade-offs without overselling.

Workshops & Collaborative Problem Solving

  • Facilitate technical workshops and brainstorming sessions with customer teams.
  • Co-design architectures and controls with customers rather than prescribing static solutions.

● Whiteboard flows covering:

○ AI access paths

○ Identity trust boundaries

○ Data movement and enforcement points

  • Use workshops to uncover real constraints and drive solution alignment.

Execution & Field Innovation

  • Troubleshoot complex issues across AI pipelines, identity flows, and data paths.
  • Create interim or custom solutions using Python, YAML, and cloud services when product features are missing.
  • Collaborate with Product and Engineering to validate feasibility and relay field feedback.
  • Maintain technical assets, demo configurations, and documentation in GitHub.

Required Skills & Experience

  • Deep, practical understanding of Data Loss Prevention (DLP):

○ Inspection, classification, enforcement points

○ Real-world limitations and bypass scenarios

● Strong hands-on knowledge of:

○ AI systems, LLMs, AI agents

○ Emerging AI security risks and abuse patterns

  • Solid foundation in Identity & Access Management (IAM):

○ SSO, OAuth/OIDC, tokens, policy enforcement

● Practical experience with:

○ Docker

○ Linux

○ Python

○ YAML-based configuration

  • Familiarity with endpoint and device trust tooling:

○ Microsoft Intune

○ Jamf Pro

  • Experience with cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, or GCP).
  • Comfortable using GitHub for code, configs, and version control.
  • Exceptional communication, storytelling, and executive-level presentation skills.
  • Ability to lead workshops, whiteboard complex systems, and drive collaborative design sessions.
  • Experience in an early startup environment preferred

What Success Looks Like

  • Customers trust you not just as a technologist, but as a strategic advisor.
  • Complex AI, identity, and DLP concepts are understood clearly at every stakeholder level.
  • POCs reflect real customer constraints, not idealized lab conditions.
  • Workshops result in alignment, not confusion.
  • Deals move forward because solutions are credible, transparent, and defensible—even as the product evolves.

Each of us, no matter what we do at Parexel, contributes to the development of a therapy that ultimately will benefit a patient. We take our work personally, we do it with empathy and we're committed to making a difference.

About Parexel

Parexel is a leading global clinical development partner delivering insights-driven clinical and consulting solutions to the life sciences industry. With 22,000+ employees worldwide, we partner with biopharmaceutical companies and research sites to design and deliver patient-focused clinical trials that broaden access and make research a care option for anyone, anywhere.

We work with focus, agility, and shared purpose - moving with urgency to address patient needs and accelerate the delivery of new therapies. We embrace bold thinking, adapt quickly to change, and continually raise the bar for the speed and quality of clinical research. We are expanding our team and seeking talented individuals to help drive industry leading innovation, With Heart.


About the Role

We are seeking a Statistical Programmer to join our team. As a Statistical Programmer, you will support the full lifecycle of clinical trial data - from dataset creation through regulatory submission - helping bring new therapies to patients faster and with greater confidence in data quality.

This position plays a key role in producing and quality-checking the programming deliverables that underpin clinical study results. You will work across multiple studies and drug programs, contributing directly to CDISC-compliant SDTM and ADaM datasets, as well as the tables, listings, and figures that inform regulatory decisions. You will collaborate closely with lead programmers, biostatisticians, and cross-functional study teams, following established SOPs and industry guidelines.

You will join a fast-paced, growth-oriented environment focused on making a meaningful impact through precise data programming, cross-functional collaboration, and consistent delivery against study timelines. With diverse teams and continuous learning opportunities, Statistical Programmers at Parexel can explore career paths and expand skills across the full breadth of clinical research programming.


Key Responsibilities

  • Perform both production and quality control (QC) programming of SDTM datasets, analysis datasets, tables, listings, and figures (TLFs) across multiple clinical trials using SAS and/or R
  • Integrate and reconcile data across multiple studies or drug programs to support portfolio-level reporting and submissions
  • Deliver programming work with minimal supervision under the direction of a lead programmer, maintaining high standards of accuracy and compliance with CDISC standards
  • Proactively communicate risks to timelines or technical issues to the lead programmer or technical lead, enabling plans to be adjusted before deadlines are impacted
  • Manage a moderate to large volume of complex programming tasks simultaneously, including ad-hoc requests, with minimal guidance
  • Participate in team meetings and maintain availability during core working hours to support effective collaboration with cross-functional stakeholders
  • Apply knowledge of ICH and FDA/EMEA guidelines and drug submission requirements to programming deliverables (Programmer II and III levels)


Candidate Profile

You will thrive in this role if you bring:

  • Strengths in SAS and/or R programming, data integration, and clinical trial dataset development
  • Experience working in a pharmaceutical, biotech, or CRO environment with exposure to regulated data standards
  • The ability to manage competing priorities, communicate proactively, and collaborate across teams
  • A detail-oriented mindset and a strong commitment to data accuracy and quality control
  • Comfort working independently with minimal supervision while knowing when to escalate
  • Familiarity with CDISC standards (SDTM, ADaM) and regulatory submission requirements

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Economics, Computer Science, Information Technology, Biology, Social Science, or a related scientific discipline
  • Programmer I: Entry-level candidates with foundational SAS and/or R programming knowledge and exposure to clinical data environments are encouraged to apply
  • Programmer II: Minimum of 3 years of SAS programming experience in the pharmaceutical or biotech industry, with extensive knowledge of CDISC standards and working knowledge of drug submission requirements and relevant ICH and FDA/EMEA guidelines
  • Programmer III: Minimum of 5 years of SAS and/or R programming experience in the pharmaceutical or biotech industry, with extensive knowledge of drug submission requirements and relevant ICH and FDA/EMEA guidelines, and deep expertise in CDISC standards
  • Strong organizational, interpersonal, and communication skills
  • Demonstrated ability to handle complex tasks and ad-hoc requests with minimal supervision

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience supporting regulatory submissions (NDA, BLA, or IND packages)
  • Familiarity with both SDTM and ADaM implementation guides
  • Experience across multiple therapeutic areas or study phases
  • Proficiency in both SAS and R programming environments

Vous avez l’esprit vif et une grande curiosité, et les acquisitions comme l’ambiguïté vous stimulent. Vous arrivez avec des solutions, vous restez calme sous pression et vous menez plusieurs dossiers de front avec agilité. Surtout, vous conseillez avec aplomb et avec tact.

jobs.description:
Job Description Summary

GE HealthCare is helping to build a world where healthcare has no limits. To get there, the way we work will be as important as what we make. This role is part of a larger transformation at GE HealthCare to redesign our end-to-end HR operating model. AI is changing how work gets done, and we need a leader who will design how our work, our organization and our workforce change with it, and who will guide our business and our people through that shift.

Reporting to the Chief People Officer and serving on the Chief People Officer’s leadership team, you will build and lead a new team responsible for workforce strategy and planning, people analytics (workforce and talent intelligence), and the design of work and organizations. This is a newly created role and one of the most important hires for the future of our People & Culture function.

Your team will own strategy, policy and program design. This includes setting the enterprise workforce strategy, building people analytics capabilities that drive insight across the organization, and creating the methods and frameworks for successful work redesign and organization design. Business and functional leaders own business outcomes. You bring the workforce and organization strategy, intelligence and design that help them deliver. You will work with business-aligned teams to apply the enterprise strategy to their unique businesses and put that work into practice, making sure they have the tools, guidance and skills to bring it to life.

Job Description

Key areas of scope

  • Workforce strategy and planning. The enterprise workforce strategy and plan; demand and supply of skills and capacity; planning for people and AI capacity together; the mix of employees, contractors and outside partners; location and footprint; workforce cost and value.
  • People analytics (workforce and talent intelligence). Workforce and talent analytics; external talent market insight; predictive signals; scenario models; and tools that help leaders make workforce decisions.
  • Work redesign and organization design. Organization and operating model design; role architecture; spans and layers; work simplification and productivity; and the redesign of work done by people and AI together.

Your first-year priorities

  • Workforce data foundation. Define the workforce data and infrastructure requirements needed to inform workforce strategy and planning over the next 12 to 24 months.
  • Enterprise workforce plan. Build the enterprise workforce strategy and plan for 2028 to 2029.
  • Playbook for the business. Create the playbook business teams use to apply the workforce plan to their own areas of the business.
  • People analytics and AI insight. Provide strategic direction as we build our digital infrastructure and AI-enabled insight into workforce capabilities, partnering with P&C technology, which builds and runs these tools.
  • Work redesign at scale. Build on our proven work redesign pilots, expand the capability across the company, and create the tools and frameworks to transform work at scale. Work redesign is the single biggest area of future value for People & Culture.

Key responsibilities

Work redesign and organization design

  • Make work redesign a core company capability, building on our existing pilots and growing it across businesses and functions.
  • Lead work redesign with a clear method: start with the outcome, understand how work really happens, design the future flow of work, then decide which tasks and decisions sit with people and which sit with technology.
  • Build the tools and frameworks to redesign work at scale, including a common list of tasks and roles, a library of proven ways for people and AI to work together, a standard for redesigned roles, and a method to measure the workforce impact of each redesign.
  • Set principles for organization and operating model design, role architecture, and spans and layers that adapt as AI changes how teams are structured.
  • Define clear roles and accountabilities across people and technology, including decision rights, where human judgment is required, quality standards and escalation paths, so teams can move quickly and people remain accountable for results.
  • Partner with technology teams on the governance of AI agents, adding a regular review of how they affect roles and the workforce.

Workforce strategy and planning

  • Turn business priorities into clear workforce goals, and own the enterprise workforce strategy and plan.
  • Plan for human and AI capacity together, modeling demand and supply of skills under different scenarios.
  • Set clear guidance on when to build, buy, borrow or automate: when to develop people, hire, use contractors or partners, or use AI and automation.
  • Protect the expertise the company needs, and strengthen pathways for early-career colleagues to build judgment as routine work changes.
  • Give leaders scenarios on location and footprint, and on workforce choices when we acquire businesses.
  • Build a clear view of workforce economics, including the full cost of the workforce, how capacity freed by automation is used, and whether expected value is actually realized.

People analytics (workforce and talent intelligence)

  • Lead people analytics, bringing together trusted people, skills, workload and performance data with business plans, colleague listening, and external talent market and competitor insight.
  • Define the data, measures and calculation rules that P&C technology needs to build workforce data and AI tools, and set how that data is governed, with strong privacy, security and responsible use.
  • Turn complex evidence into clear, decision-ready recommendations for the Chief People Officer, executives and business teams. Explain choices and uncertainty plainly, without overstating precision.
  • Move from looking back to looking ahead: build predictive signals that tell leaders when to act, and scenario models that show the trade-offs of each choice.

Influence and capability building

  • Build the capability of business-aligned teams to apply workforce strategy, planning and work redesign, through playbooks, tools, coaching and training.
  • Make clear who decides what on workforce and organization changes, and how decisions with effects beyond one business are escalated.
  • Partner closely with the Talent, Capability & Change team, Total Rewards, P&C technology, Finance and business unit leaders.
  • Be a trusted advisor to the Chief People Officer and senior leaders on how AI will change work and the workforce, and what to do about it.

How success will be measured

We will track early signals, such as readiness, decision speed and how quickly capacity moves to higher-value work, and connect them to lasting results that matter to the business, including:

  • Capability readiness. The workforce capabilities we need for our highest-priority work are in place before gaps slow us down.
  • Workforce value. Work, roles, structure and automation are designed so capacity shifts toward the highest-value work.
  • Faster, better decisions. Trusted workforce data and clear trade-offs lead to faster, better people and organization decisions.

Basic qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree.
  • 12+ years of progressive leadership experience in workforce strategy, workforce planning, organization design, people analytics or HR strategy, in a company or as a consultant.
  • Proven experience leading enterprise-wide workforce planning or work redesign in a large, global organization.
  • Experience using data and analytics to shape senior leaders’ decisions about the workforce and the organization.
  • A track record of building new teams and capabilities, and of leading through influence with senior executives.

Preferred qualifications

  • HR leadership experience in a large, global company. Strategy consulting experience will also be considered.
  • Hands-on experience redesigning work and roles for AI and automation, at scale.
  • Experience building a people analytics or workforce intelligence function, including predictive models and scenario planning.
  • Experience with workforce economics and close partnership with Finance.
  • Master’s degree or MBA.

What will make you successful

  • You design for the future, not the past. You can picture how work should look and build the path to get there.
  • You are a builder. You are comfortable starting with a blank page and creating a team, methods and tools.
  • You make complex ideas simple, without hiding how much work it takes to put them in place.
  • You lead through influence. You get results through teams and leaders you do not manage.
  • You balance people and business needs. When trade-offs are needed, you keep business results first.

The Field Operations Manager leads regional teams of Field Adjusters responsible for on-site damage appraisals, automotive mechanical inspections, repair authorization assessments, risk evaluations, and repair recommendations. The ideal candidate brings strong leadership and communication skills, experience in insurance, automotive dealership operations, and risk management, and the ability to build trusted dealer relationships, navigate escalations, and maintain high standards for accuracy and service quality.

The Work Itself

Field Operations & Claims Servicing

  • Lead multiple regional field teams responsible for timely, accurate Dealer Open Lot weather claim damage appraisals and F&I mechanical inspections and authorizations, ensuring consistent execution and responsiveness across geographies.
  • Maintain operational readiness for changing claim volumes, including weather-event surge capacity, territory coverage, workload balancing, and inspection resource deployment.

People Leadership & Development

  • Lead, coach, and develop Field Supervisors while creating clear expectations for quality, service, accountability, technical proficiency, and team engagement.
  • Build the capabilities of field adjusters through coaching, calibration, training, knowledge sharing, and development opportunities strengthening the field organization.

Culture, Engagement & Organizational Leadership

  • Build an engaged, accountable field culture centered on dealer service, claim quality, sound judgment, and continuous improvement.
  • Represent Field Operations as a leadership voice, connecting strategy to frontline execution and ensuring supervisors and adjusters understand the why, expectations, and business outcomes behind organizational change.

Dealer & Customer Experience

  • Serve as a management escalation point for complex or sensitive claims, bringing together the appropriate field, office, underwriting, and business partners to establish a clear path to resolution.

Quality, Controls & Financial Stewardship

  • Drive inspection and claim quality through file reviews, quality calibration, policy adherence, and consistent application of coverage and estimating standards.

Supplier & Vendor Management

  • Oversee field inspection suppliers and vendor relationships, establishing clear expectations for service levels, inspection quality, cycle time, capacity, geographic coverage, and escalation management.

Cross-Functional Alignment

Strategy, Innovation & Continuous Improvement
